+ nb.metadata['language_info'] = {'name': 'python', 'version': '3.9.0'}
+ cells = []
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "# Tutorial 03 - Empirical Covariance Estimation &amp; Model Fitting\n\n"
+ "**Package:** stamps_v3  \n"
+ "**MATLAB equivalent:** &#96;STATLIBtutorial.m&#96; §4-end  \n"
+ "**Dataset:** Falmagne soil dataset\n\n"
+ "---\n\n"
+ "## Learning objectives\n\n"
+ "1. Compute **empirical spatial covariance** with &#96;stcov&#96;.\n"
+ "2. Fit a nested covariance model by **Weighted Least Squares (WLS)** with &#96;covmodelfit&#96;.\n"
+ "3. Fit a **Linear Model of Coregionalisation (LMC)** for three variables "
+ "(sand, silt, clay) using &#96;coregfit&#96;.\n"
+ "4. Apply **Normal Score Transformation (NST)** with &#96;other2gauss&#96; and repeat "
+ "the covariance workflow on the transformed data.\n\n"
+ "### Key difference from MATLAB\n\n"
+ "&gt; MATLAB's &#96;vario()&#96; computes the **variogram** $\\gamma(h) = \\frac{1}{2}\\text{E}[Z(\\mathbf{s}+\\mathbf{h})-Z(\\mathbf{s})]^2$.  \n"
+ "&gt; stamps_v3's &#96;stcov()&#96; computes the **covariance** $C(h) = \\text{Cov}[Z(\\mathbf{s}), Z(\\mathbf{s}+\\mathbf{h})]$.  \n"
+ "&gt; They are related by $C(h) = C(0) - \\gamma(h)$, but stamps uses covariances throughout.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "import sys, os, pickle\n"
+ "import numpy as np\n"
+ "import pandas as pd\n"
+ "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n"
+ "REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), '..'))\n"

+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 1. Empirical spatial covariance with &#96;stcov&#96;\n\n"
+ "&#96;stcov&#96; computes the empirical covariance for each spatial lag class defined by "
+ "&#96;lagS&#96; (lag centres) and &#96;lagS_range&#96; (half-widths).\n\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n"
+ "lagCOVv, lagCOVn, lagSS, lagTT = stcov(\n"
+ "    grid_s, grid_t, grid_v,\n"
+ "    lagS, lagS_range,\n"
+ "    lagT=None, lagT_range=None   # omit for pure-spatial case\n"
+ ")\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n"
+ "**Return values:**\n"
+ "- &#96;lagCOVv&#96; — empirical covariance values\n"
+ "- &#96;lagCOVn&#96; — number of pairs per lag class\n"
+ "- &#96;lagSS&#96;, &#96;lagTT&#96; — spatial and temporal lag centres\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Spatial lag settings (in metres)\n"
+ "lagS       = np.arange(0, 13_500, 500.0)   # lag centres 0..13000 m\n"
+ "lagS_range = np.full(len(lagS), 500.0)      # half-width 500 m\n\n"
+ "# For pure-spatial stcov, wrap data as 2-D (grid_s=coords, grid_t=dummy, grid_v=data)\n"
+ "# stcov expects grid_s: (ns,d), grid_t: (nt,), grid_v: (ns, nt)\n"
+ "grid_s = ch                           # (118, 2)\n"
+ "grid_t = np.array([0.0])              # single time step\n"
+ "grid_v = sand[:, np.newaxis]          # (118, 1)\n\n"
+ "lagCOVv, lagCOVn, lagSS, lagTT = stcov(\n"
+ "    grid_s, grid_t, grid_v,\n"
+ "    lagS, lagS_range,\n"
+ ")\n\n"
+ "# Extract the 1-D spatial covariance profile\n"
+ "lag_h = lagSS.ravel()     # spatial lag values\n"
+ "cov_h = lagCOVv.ravel()   # covariance at each lag\n"
+ "n_h   = lagCOVn.ravel()   # number of pairs\n\n"
+ "# Remove empty bins\n"
+ "valid = (n_h &gt; 0) &amp; ~np.isnan(cov_h)\n"
+ "lag_h, cov_h, n_h = lag_h[valid], cov_h[valid], n_h[valid]\n\n"
+ "print(f'Lag range  : {lag_h.min():.0f} - {lag_h.max():.0f} m')\n"
+ "print(f'C(0)       : {cov_h[0]:.4f}')\n"
+ "print(f'Lag bins used: {valid.sum()}')\n"
+ ))

+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4))\n\n"

+ "axes[0].set_title('Empirical covariance - Sand')\n\n"

+ "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"

+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 2. Fitting a nested covariance model by WLS\n\n"
+ "&#96;covmodelfit&#96; minimises the weighted sum of squared residuals between the "
+ "empirical covariance values and the model prediction:\n\n"
+ r"$$\text{WSS} = \sum_k n_k \left[\hat{C}(h_k) - C_{\text{model}}(h_k)\right]^2$$"
+ "\n\nwhere $n_k$ is the number of pairs used to estimate $\\hat{C}(h_k)$.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Nested model: nugget + spherical\n"
+ "# covparam0 = initial guesses: [sill0], [sill1, range1]\n"
+ "covmodel  = ['nuggetC', 'sphericalC']\n"
+ "covparam0 = [(20.0,), (80.0, 5_000.0)]\n\n"
+ "# covmodelfit expects:\n"
+ "#   covmodelfit(lag_cov_s, lag_cov_t, lag_cov_v, lag_cov_n, covmodel, covparam0)\n"
+ "lag_cov_s = lag_h.reshape(-1, 1)    # (n_valid, 1) spatial lags\n"
+ "lag_cov_t = np.array([[0.0]])        # (1, 1) dummy time lag\n"
+ "lag_cov_v = cov_h.reshape(-1, 1)    # (n_valid, 1) empirical covariances\n"
+ "lag_cov_n = n_h.reshape(-1, 1)      # (n_valid, 1) pair counts\n\n"
+ "result = covmodelfit(lag_cov_s, lag_cov_t, lag_cov_v, lag_cov_n,\n"
+ "                     covmodel, covparam0)\n"
+ "fitted_covparam = result['covparam']\n"
+ "print('Fitted parameters:')\n"
+ "for m, p in zip(covmodel, fitted_covparam):\n"
+ "    print(f'  {m}: {np.array(p).round(2)}')\n"

+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "from stamps.models.covmodel import nuggetC, sphericalC\n\n"
+ "h_plot = np.linspace(0, lag_h.max(), 300)\n"
+ "C_fitted = (nuggetC(h_plot, *fitted_covparam[0])\n"

+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4))\n\n"
+ "axes[0].plot(lag_h / 1000, cov_h,   'o', color='steelblue', ms=5, label='Empirical')\n"
+ "axes[0].plot(h_plot / 1000, C_fitted, '-', color='tomato',   lw=2,  label='Fitted model')\n"

+ "axes[0].set_title('Sand covariance: empirical vs fitted'); axes[0].legend()\n\n"

+ "axes[1].set_xlabel('Lag (km)'); axes[1].set_ylabel('gamma(h)')\n"
+ "axes[1].set_title('Equivalent variogram: empirical vs fitted'); axes[1].legend()\n\n"
+ "for ax in axes: ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"

+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 3. Empirical covariance for silt and clay\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "def compute_stcov_1d(ch, z, lagS, lagS_range):\n"
+ "    '''Helper: compute 1-D empirical covariance for a single variable.'''\n"
+ "    grid_v = z[:, np.newaxis]\n"
+ "    grid_t = np.array([0.0])\n"
+ "    lagCOVv, lagCOVn, lagSS, _ = stcov(ch, grid_t, grid_v, lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "    h   = lagSS.ravel()\n"
+ "    C   = lagCOVv.ravel()\n"
+ "    n   = lagCOVn.ravel()\n"
+ "    ok  = (n &gt; 0) &amp; ~np.isnan(C)\n"
+ "    return h[ok], C[ok], n[ok]\n\n\n"
+ "lag_s_silt, cov_silt, n_silt = compute_stcov_1d(ch, silt, lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "lag_s_clay, cov_clay, n_clay = compute_stcov_1d(ch, clay, lagS, lagS_range)\n\n"
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 4))\n"
+ "data_list = [('Sand', lag_h,     cov_h,     'steelblue'),\n"
+ "             ('Silt', lag_s_silt, cov_silt, 'goldenrod'),\n"
+ "             ('Clay', lag_s_clay, cov_clay, 'tomato')]\n\n"
+ "for ax, (name, lh, ch_cov, col) in zip(axes, data_list):\n"
+ "    ax.plot(lh / 1000, ch_cov, 'o', color=col, ms=5)\n"
+ "    ax.axhline(0, color='gray', ls='--', lw=0.8)\n"
+ "    ax.set_xlabel('Lag (km)'); ax.set_ylabel('Covariance')\n"
+ "    ax.set_title(f'{name} - empirical covariance'); ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)\n\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 4. Linear Model of Coregionalisation (LMC) with &#96;coregfit&#96;\n\n"
+ "When working with multiple co-located variables, we need a **jointly valid** "
+ "cross-covariance model.  The LMC assumes:\n\n"
+ r"$$C_{ij}(h) = \sum_{u=1}^{U} b^{(u)}_{ij}\, g_u(h)$$"
+ "\n\nwhere $g_u(h)$ are basic covariance models and "
+ r"$\mathbf{B}^{(u)} = [b^{(u)}_{ij}]$ are positive semi-definite **coregionalisation matrices**."
+ "\n\n"
+ "&#96;coregfit&#96; uses Iterated Alternating Weighted Least Squares (IALS) to estimate "
+ "the $\\mathbf{B}^{(u)}$ matrices jointly.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Build a 3-variable empirical cross-covariance structure\n"
+ "# d[k,l] = lag, V[k,l] = covariance of variable pair (k,l)\n"
+ "# We stack the three variables and compute pairwise covariances\n\n"
+ "variables_all  = np.column_stack([sand, silt, clay])  # (118, 3)\n"
+ "nv = 3\n\n"
+ "# Compute empirical covariance for all 6 unique pairs (including auto-covariances)\n"
+ "pair_names = ['Sand-Sand', 'Silt-Silt', 'Clay-Clay',\n"
+ "              'Sand-Silt', 'Sand-Clay', 'Silt-Clay']\n"
+ "pair_idx   = [(0,0), (1,1), (2,2), (0,1), (0,2), (1,2)]\n\n"
+ "cov_data = {}\n"
+ "for (i, j), name in zip(pair_idx, pair_names):\n"
+ "    # Cross-covariance: compute product of mean-centred values\n"
+ "    zi = variables_all[:, i] - variables_all[:, i].mean()\n"
+ "    zj = variables_all[:, j] - variables_all[:, j].mean()\n"
+ "    # Use stcov on the pairwise product as a proxy\n"
+ "    prod_ij = (zi * zj)[:, np.newaxis]\n"
+ "    lh, _, n = compute_stcov_1d(ch, (variables_all[:, i] + variables_all[:, j]) / 2,\n"
+ "                                 lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "    # Proper cross-covariance via manual lag binning\n"
+ "    lh_i, cv_i, _ = compute_stcov_1d(ch, variables_all[:, i], lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "    lh_j, cv_j, _ = compute_stcov_1d(ch, variables_all[:, j], lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "    # For same lag bins, approximate cross-cov from individual stcov calls\n"
+ "    # (true cross-cov needs the paired product; use correlation-weighted estimate)\n"
+ "    cov_data[name] = (lh_i, cv_i)\n\n"
+ "# For coregfit we build stacked D and V matrices across lags\n"
+ "# D: (n_lags,) lag values shared, V: (nv, nv, n_lags) cross-covariance tensor\n"
+ "# Here we use the auto-covariances on the diagonal and 0 off-diagonal (simplification)\n"
+ "n_lags = len(lag_h)\n"
+ "D_arr  = lag_h                                      # shared lag axis\n\n"
+ "# Build cross-covariance matrix at each lag\n"
+ "# For a proper implementation, compute pairwise cross-covariances\n"
+ "# using the 'difference' method or moment estimator\n"
+ "V_tensor = np.zeros((nv, nv, n_lags))\n"
+ "for vi, var in enumerate([sand, silt, clay]):\n"
+ "    lh_vi, cv_vi, _ = compute_stcov_1d(ch, var, lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "    n_common = min(n_lags, len(cv_vi))\n"
+ "    V_tensor[vi, vi, :n_common] = cv_vi[:n_common]\n\n"
+ "# Compute cross-covariances using the linear combination trick:\n"
+ "# C_XY = 0.5*(C_(X+Y) - C_X - C_Y)\n"
+ "pairs_xy = [(0,1,'sand_silt'), (0,2,'sand_clay'), (1,2,'silt_clay')]\n"
+ "var_arrays = [sand, silt, clay]\n"
+ "for (i, j, _) in pairs_xy:\n"
+ "    zi = var_arrays[i]; zj = var_arrays[j]\n"
+ "    _, cv_sum, _ = compute_stcov_1d(ch, zi + zj, lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "    _, cv_i,   _ = compute_stcov_1d(ch, zi,       lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "    _, cv_j,   _ = compute_stcov_1d(ch, zj,       lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "    n_c = min(n_lags, len(cv_sum), len(cv_i), len(cv_j))\n"
+ "    V_tensor[i, j, :n_c] = 0.5 * (cv_sum[:n_c] - cv_i[:n_c] - cv_j[:n_c])\n"
+ "    V_tensor[j, i, :n_c] = V_tensor[i, j, :n_c]  # symmetry\n\n"
+ "print('Cross-covariance tensor shape:', V_tensor.shape)\n"
+ "print('C(0) matrix (variance-covariance at lag 0):')\n"
+ "print(np.round(V_tensor[:, :, 0], 2))\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Fit LMC: nugget + spherical structure\n"
+ "lmc_model  = ['nuggetC', 'sphericalC']\n"
+ "lmc_param0 = [(10.0,), (50.0, 5_000.0)]\n\n"
+ "# coregfit(d, V, o, model, param0)\n"
+ "# d: (n_lags,) lag values\n"
+ "# V: (nv, nv, n_lags) cross-covariance tensor\n"
+ "# o: (n_lags,) weights (use pair counts, approximate here)\n"
+ "o_weights = n_h.copy()   # use sand pair counts as weights\n\n"
+ "lmc_result = coregfit(D_arr, V_tensor, o_weights, lmc_model, lmc_param0)\n\n"
+ "print('LMC fitting result:')\n"
+ "for s in lmc_result:\n"
+ "    print(f'  Structure: {s[\"model\"]}')\n"

+ "    if 'range_param' in s:\n"
+ "        print(f'    Range: {s[\"range_param\"]:.1f} m')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Visualise fitted LMC: diagonal auto-covariances\n"
+ "from stamps.models.covmodel import nuggetC, sphericalC\n\n"
+ "h_plot = np.linspace(0, D_arr.max(), 300)\n\n"
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4))\n"
+ "varnames = ['Sand', 'Silt', 'Clay']\n"
+ "colors_v = ['steelblue', 'goldenrod', 'tomato']\n\n"
+ "for vi, (ax, vname, col) in enumerate(zip(axes, varnames, colors_v)):\n"

+ "    # Fitted LMC diagonal\n"
+ "    C_fit = np.zeros(len(h_plot))\n"
+ "    for s in lmc_result:\n"
+ "        fn   = nuggetC if s['model'] == 'nuggetC' else sphericalC\n"
+ "        b_ii = s['sill_matrix'][vi, vi]\n"
+ "        rp   = s.get('range_param', None)\n"

+ "            C_fit += fn(h_plot, b_ii)\n"
+ "        else:\n"
+ "            C_fit += fn(h_plot, b_ii, rp)\n\n"
+ "    ax.plot(h_plot / 1000, C_fit, '-', color='k', lw=2, label='LMC fit')\n"
+ "    ax.set_xlabel('Lag (km)'); ax.set_ylabel('Covariance')\n"
+ "    ax.set_title(f'{vname}: empirical vs LMC'); ax.legend(); ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)\n\n"
+ "plt.suptitle('LMC diagonal auto-covariances', fontsize=12, y=1.01)\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 5. Normal Score Transformation (NST)\n\n"
+ "Many geostatistical methods (especially BME) assume **Gaussian marginals**.  "
+ "The Normal Score Transformation maps the original data $z$ to a Gaussian "
+ "variable $y$ via the empirical CDF:\n\n"
+ r"$$y_i = \Phi^{-1}\!\left[\hat{F}(z_i)\right]$$"
+ "\n\n"
+ "After transformation, we can fit a covariance model in Gaussian space and "
+ "back-transform the results.\n\n"
+ "&#96;stamps.bme.bme_transform.other2gauss&#96; implements this using a reference CDF "
+ "(either empirical or user-supplied).\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Normal Score Transform for sand\n"
+ "# other2gauss(z, yfile, cdfyfile)\n"
+ "# yfile    : reference y values (Gaussian quantiles)\n"
+ "# cdfyfile : corresponding CDF values\n\n"
+ "# Build empirical CDF for sand\n"
+ "z_sorted = np.sort(sand)\n"
+ "n        = len(z_sorted)\n"
+ "p_vals   = (np.arange(1, n + 1) - 0.5) / n    # Hazen plotting position\n\n"
+ "from scipy.stats import norm\n"
+ "y_gauss = norm.ppf(p_vals)                      # Gaussian quantiles\n\n"
+ "# Apply NST via other2gauss\n"
+ "sand_nst = other2gauss(sand, z_sorted, p_vals)\n\n"
+ "print(f'Original sand: mean={sand.mean():.2f}, std={sand.std():.2f}')\n"
+ "print(f'NST sand:      mean={sand_nst.mean():.4f}, std={sand_nst.std():.4f}')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(16, 4))\n\n"
+ "# Histogram comparison\n"
+ "ax = axes[0]\n"
+ "ax.hist(sand,     bins=20, density=True, color='steelblue', alpha=0.6, label='Original')\n"
+ "ax.hist(sand_nst, bins=20, density=True, color='tomato',    alpha=0.6, label='NST')\n"
+ "h_ax = np.linspace(-3.5, 3.5, 200)\n"
+ "ax.plot(h_ax, norm.pdf(h_ax), 'k-', lw=2, label='N(0,1)')\n"
+ "ax.set_xlabel('Value'); ax.set_ylabel('Density')\n"
+ "ax.set_title('Sand: before vs after NST'); ax.legend()\n\n"
+ "# Scatter: original vs transformed\n"

+ "ax.scatter(sand, sand_nst, s=15, alpha=0.6, color='steelblue')\n"

+ "ax.set_title('NST transformation curve'); ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)\n\n"
+ "# Empirical covariance in transformed space\n"
+ "lh_nst, cov_nst, n_nst = compute_stcov_1d(ch, sand_nst, lagS, lagS_range)\n"
+ "ax = axes[2]\n"
+ "ax.plot(lag_h / 1000,  cov_h,   'o', color='steelblue', ms=5, label='Original sand')\n"
+ "ax.plot(lh_nst / 1000, cov_nst, 's', color='tomato',    ms=5, label='NST sand')\n"
+ "ax.axhline(0, color='gray', ls='--', lw=0.8)\n"
+ "ax.set_xlabel('Lag (km)'); ax.set_ylabel('Covariance')\n"
+ "ax.set_title('Covariance: original vs NST sand'); ax.legend()\n\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+

+ "lag_cov_s_nst = lh_nst.reshape(-1, 1)\n\n"

+ "                         lag_cov_v_nst, lag_cov_n_nst,\n"

+ "C_nst_fitted = (nuggetC(h_plot, *fitted_nst[0])\n"

+ "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))\n"

+ "ax.plot(h_plot / 1000, C_nst_fitted, '-', color='k',     lw=2,  label='NST fitted')\n"
+ "ax.set_xlabel('Lag (km)'); ax.set_ylabel('Covariance')\n"
+ "ax.set_title('NST sand: empirical covariance + fitted model'); ax.legend()\n"
+ "ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3); plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"
+ ))

+ "import pickle\n\n"
+ "cov_params = {\n"

+ "    'sand_nst_covmodel': ['nuggetC', 'sphericalC'],\n"

+ # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+ """Generate 04_kriging_and_cokriging.ipynb"""

+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "# Tutorial 04 - Kriging, Cokriging &amp; Kriging with Transformation\n\n"
+ "**Package:** stamps_v3  \n"
+ "**MATLAB equivalent:** &#96;BMEHRLIBtutorial.m&#96;  \n"
+ "**Dataset:** Falmagne soil dataset\n\n"
+ "---\n\n"
+ "## Learning objectives\n\n"
+ "1. Apply **ordinary kriging** of sand content on a 17 x 19 grid.\n"
+ "2. Apply **multivariate cokriging** jointly exploiting sand + silt + clay.\n"
+ "3. Apply **cokriging with transformation** (&#96;cokrigingT&#96;) in Normal-Score space "
+ "followed by back-transformation to original units.\n"
+ "4. Compare the three methods side-by-side.\n\n"
+ "### Kriging in stamps_v3\n\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n"

+ "- &#96;ch&#96;       — data coordinates        (nh, d)\n"
+ "- &#96;zh&#96;       — data values             (nh,)\n"
+ "- &#96;covmodel&#96; — model name(s)\n"
+ "- &#96;covparam&#96; — model parameter(s)\n"
+ "- &#96;nhmax&#96;    — max neighbours\n"
+ "- &#96;dmax&#96;     — max search radius\n"
+ "- &#96;order&#96;    — 0=ordinary, None=simple kriging\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "import sys, os, pickle\n"
+ "import numpy as np\n"
+ "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n"
+ "REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), '..'))\n"
+ "if REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:\n"
+ "    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)\n\n"
+ "from stamps.stest.kriging import kriging, cokriging, cokrigingT\n\n"

+ "# Load dataset\n"
+ "with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'tutorial01_data.pkl'), 'rb') as f:\n"

+ "print('Data loaded:', ch.shape, '  Grid:', ck.shape)\n"

+ "for m, p in zip(cov['sand_covmodel'], cov['sand_covparam']):\n"
+ "    print(f'  {m}: {np.round(p, 2)}')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 1. Ordinary kriging of sand content\n\n"
+ "Ordinary kriging (OK) minimises the estimation error variance under the "
+ "constraint that the weights sum to 1 (unbiasedness).  "
+ "It requires only the covariance model of the target variable.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Kriging parameters\n"
+ "covmodel = cov['sand_covmodel']    # ['nuggetC', 'sphericalC']\n"
+ "covparam = cov['sand_covparam']    # [(c0,), (c1, a1)]\n"
+ "nhmax    = 25                       # max neighbours\n"
+ "dmax     = 10_000.0                 # 10 km search radius\n"
+ "order    = 0                        # ordinary kriging\n\n"
+ "print('Running ordinary kriging...')\n"
+ "zk_mean, zk_var = kriging(ck, ch, sand, covmodel, covparam, nhmax, dmax, order)\n"
+ "print(f'Estimated {np.sum(~np.isnan(zk_mean))} / {len(ck)} nodes')\n"
+ "print(f'Mean estimate : {np.nanmean(zk_mean):.2f}%')\n"
+ "print(f'Mean var      : {np.nanmean(zk_var):.4f}')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "def plot_map(ax, ck, zk, title, n_e, n_n, cmap='hot_r',\n"
+ "             ch_data=None, data_vals=None, vmin=None, vmax=None, cbar_label=''):\n"
+ "    eu = np.unique(ck[:, 0]); nu = np.unique(ck[:, 1])\n"
+ "    Z  = zk.reshape(n_n, n_e)\n"
+ "    vm = vmin if vmin is not None else np.nanpercentile(zk, 2)\n"
+ "    vx = vmax if vmax is not None else np.nanpercentile(zk, 98)\n"
+ "    im = ax.pcolormesh(eu, nu, Z, cmap=cmap, vmin=vm, vmax=vx, shading='nearest')\n"
+ "    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label=cbar_label)\n"
+ "    if ch_data is not None and data_vals is not None:\n"
+ "        ax.scatter(ch_data[:, 0], ch_data[:, 1], c=data_vals, cmap=cmap,\n"
+ "                   vmin=vm, vmax=vx, edgecolors='k', lw=0.5, s=45, zorder=3)\n"
+ "    ax.set_title(title); ax.set_aspect('equal')\n"
+ "    ax.set_xlabel('Easting (m)'); ax.set_ylabel('Northing (m)')\n\n\n"
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))\n"
+ "vlo, vhi = 0, 60\n"
+ "plot_map(axes[0], ck, zk_mean, 'OK mean - Sand (%)',\n"
+ "         n_e, n_n, ch_data=ch, data_vals=sand, vmin=vlo, vmax=vhi, cbar_label='Sand (%)')\n"
+ "plot_map(axes[1], ck, zk_var,  'OK variance',\n"
+ "         n_e, n_n, cmap='Blues', cbar_label='Variance')\n"
+ "plt.suptitle('Ordinary Kriging - Sand content', fontsize=12, y=1.01)\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 2. Multivariate cokriging\n\n"
+ "Cokriging jointly uses all three variables (sand, silt, clay) to improve estimation.  "
+ "It relies on the **LMC** (Linear Model of Coregionalisation) fitted in Tutorial 03.\n\n"
+ "The cokriging system builds a joint $(n_{sand} + n_{silt} + n_{clay}) \\times "
+ "(n_{sand} + n_{silt} + n_{clay})$ covariance matrix.\n\n"
+ "**stamps_v3 signature:**\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n"
+ "zk_mean, zk_var = cokriging(\n"
+ "    ck, ch, ch_var, zh,\n"
+ "    models, params, nhmax, dmax, order\n"
+ ")\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;\n"
+ "- &#96;ch_var&#96; — variable index for each data point (0=sand, 1=silt, 2=clay)\n"
+ "- &#96;models&#96;/&#96;params&#96; — LMC model names and parameters (sill matrices + ranges)\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Prepare cokriging inputs\n"
+ "# Stack all three variables with their variable index\n"
+ "n_pts = len(ch)\n"
+ "ch_all  = np.vstack([ch, ch, ch])                   # (3n, 2) repeated coords\n"
+ "zh_all  = np.concatenate([sand, silt, clay])         # (3n,) values\n"
+ "var_all = np.concatenate([np.zeros(n_pts, dtype=int),  # 0 = sand\n"
+ "                           np.ones(n_pts,  dtype=int),  # 1 = silt\n"

+ "cok_params = []\n"
+ "for s in lmc_result:\n"

+ "        cok_params.append((s['sill_matrix'], s['range_param']))\n"
+ "    else:\n"
+ "        cok_params.append((s['sill_matrix'],))\n\n"
+ "print('Cokriging models:', cok_models)\n"
+ "print('Sill matrix of spherical structure:')\n"
+ "print(np.round(lmc_result[-1]['sill_matrix'], 2))\n\n"
+ "print('\\nRunning cokriging...')\n"
+ "zk_cok_mean, zk_cok_var = cokriging(\n"
+ "    ck, ch_all, var_all, zh_all,\n"
+ "    cok_models, cok_params,\n"
+ "    nhmax=15, dmax=10_000.0, order=0\n"
+ ")\n"

+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))\n"
+ "plot_map(axes[0], ck, zk_cok_mean, 'Cokriging mean - Sand (%)',\n"
+ "         n_e, n_n, ch_data=ch, data_vals=sand, vmin=vlo, vmax=vhi, cbar_label='Sand (%)')\n"
+ "plot_map(axes[1], ck, zk_cok_var,  'Cokriging variance',\n"
+ "         n_e, n_n, cmap='Blues', cbar_label='Variance')\n"
+ "plt.suptitle('Multivariate Cokriging - Sand content', fontsize=12, y=1.01)\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"

+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 3. Kriging with Normal Score Transformation (&#96;cokrigingT&#96;)\n\n"
+ "&#96;cokrigingT&#96; performs the full NST workflow automatically:\n\n"
+ "1. Transform all input data to Gaussian scores using the reference CDF.\n"
+ "2. Run cokriging in Gaussian space.\n"
+ "3. Back-transform the kriged Gaussian mean/variance to original units.\n\n"
+ "This is the recommended workflow when the data is significantly non-Gaussian.\n\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n"
+ "zk_mean, zk_var = cokrigingT(\n"
+ "    ck, ch, ch_var, yh,\n"
+ "    models, params, nhmax, dmax,\n"
+ "    yfile, cdfyfile   # reference CDF for back-transformation\n"
+ ")\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Build reference CDF for sand (from Tutorial 03)\n"
+ "z_sorted = cov['sand_z_sorted']   # sorted original sand values\n"

+ "# NST covariance model (fitted in Tutorial 03)\n"

+ "nst_param  = cov['sand_nst_covparam']\n\n"
+ "print('NST covariance model:', nst_model)\n"
+ "print('NST parameters:', [np.round(p, 4) for p in nst_param])\n\n"
+ "# For cokrigingT with a single variable, set all var indices to 0\n"
+ "var_sand = np.zeros(n_pts, dtype=int)\n\n"
+ "print('Running cokrigingT (with NST)...')\n"
+ "zk_nst_mean, zk_nst_var = cokrigingT(\n"
+ "    ck, ch, var_sand, sand,\n"
+ "    nst_model, nst_param,\n"
+ "    nhmax=25, dmax=10_000.0,\n"
+ "    yfile=z_sorted, cdfyfile=p_vals\n"
+ ")\n"
+ "print(f'cokrigingT: {np.sum(~np.isnan(zk_nst_mean))} / {len(ck)} nodes estimated')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(14, 5))\n"
+ "plot_map(axes[0], ck, zk_nst_mean, 'KrigingT mean - Sand (%)',\n"
+ "         n_e, n_n, ch_data=ch, data_vals=sand, vmin=vlo, vmax=vhi, cbar_label='Sand (%)')\n"
+ "plot_map(axes[1], ck, zk_nst_var,  'KrigingT variance',\n"
+ "         n_e, n_n, cmap='Blues', cbar_label='Variance')\n"
+ "plt.suptitle('Kriging with NST Back-Transformation', fontsize=12, y=1.01)\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"

+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell("## 4. Three-way comparison"))

+ "vars_ = [zk_var,  zk_cok_var,  zk_nst_var]\n\n"
+ "for i, (mu, va, tm, tv) in enumerate(zip(means, vars_, titles_mean, titles_var)):\n"

+ "             ch_data=ch, data_vals=sand, vmin=vlo, vmax=vhi, cbar_label='Sand (%)')\n"
+ "    plot_map(axes[1, i], ck, va, tv, n_e, n_n,\n"
+ "             cmap='Blues', cbar_label='Variance')\n\n"

+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(

+

+ "    plot_map(ax, ck, zk_m, f'OK  dmax={dv//1000} km',\n"

+ "             vmin=vlo, vmax=vhi, cbar_label='Sand (%)')\n\n"

+ "plt.tight_layout(); plt.show()\n"

+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(

+ "    'zk_ok_var':   zk_var,\n"

+ "    pickle.dump(krig_results, f)\n"
+ "print('Saved:', save_path)\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 6. Summary\n\n"
+ "| Method | Variables used | Error variance vs OK |\n"
+ "|---|---|---|\n"
+ "| Ordinary Kriging | Sand only | Baseline |\n"
+ "| Cokriging | Sand + Silt + Clay | Lower (cross-correlation exploited) |\n"
+ "| KrigingT | Sand (via NST) | Similar to OK but Gaussian in transformed space |\n\n"
+ "**Key insights:**\n"
+ "- Cokriging reduces estimation variance when auxiliary variables are correlated with the target.\n"
+ "- &#96;cokrigingT&#96; is preferred when the marginal distribution is strongly non-Gaussian (e.g., right-skewed).\n"

+ "**Next:** Tutorial 05 — BME with interval soft data.\n"

+ # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+ """Generate 05_bme_interval_soft_data.ipynb"""
+ import nbformat as nbf
+ 
+ nb = nbf.v4.new_notebook()
+ nb.metadata['kernelspec'] = {'display_name': 'Python 3', 'language': 'python', 'name': 'python3'}
+ nb.metadata['language_info'] = {'name': 'python', 'version': '3.9.0'}
+ cells = []
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "# Tutorial 05 - BME with Interval (Soft) Data\n\n"
+ "**Package:** stamps_v3  \n"
+ "**MATLAB equivalent:** &#96;BMEINTLIBtutorial.m&#96;  \n"
+ "**Dataset:** Falmagne interval dataset (&#96;IntervalData.txt&#96;)\n\n"
+ "---\n\n"
+ "## Learning objectives\n\n"
+ "1. Load and explore the Falmagne **interval soft data** dataset.\n"
+ "2. Encode interval observations as **uniform soft PDFs** with &#96;probaUniform&#96;.\n"
+ "3. Run **BME posterior-moments** estimation with &#96;BMEPosteriorMoments&#96;.\n"
+ "4. Compare the BME result to the ordinary kriging estimate from Tutorial 04.\n\n"
+ "### What is interval (soft) data?\n\n"
+ "Instead of knowing the exact sand content at a location, we know only that "
+ "it falls within an interval $[z^{lo}, z^{up}]$.  "
+ "BME encodes this as a **uniform probability density** over the interval.\n\n"
+ "$$f(z) = \\begin{cases} \\frac{1}{z^{up} - z^{lo}} &amp; z^{lo} \\le z \\le z^{up} \\\\\n"
+ "         0 &amp; \\text{otherwise} \\end{cases}$$\n\n"
+ "This is a *soft* measurement: less informative than a precise value "
+ "but more informative than knowing nothing.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "import sys, os, pickle\n"
+ "import numpy as np\n"
+ "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n"
+ "REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), '..'))\n"
+ "if REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:\n"
+ "    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)\n\n"
+ "from stamps.bme.softconverter import probaUniform, proba2stat\n"
+ "from stamps.bme.BMEprobaEstimations import BMEPosteriorMoments\n\n"
+ "plt.rcParams.update({'figure.dpi': 110, 'font.size': 10})\n"
+ "DATA_DIR = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'data')\n\n"
+ "# Load hard data and grid from Tutorial 01\n"
+ "with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'tutorial01_data.pkl'), 'rb') as f:\n"
+ "    d1 = pickle.load(f)\n"
+ "ch   = d1['ch']\n"
+ "sand = d1['sand']\n"
+ "ck   = d1['ck']\n"
+ "n_e  = d1['n_e']\n"
+ "n_n  = d1['n_n']\n\n"
+ "# Load covariance model from Tutorial 03\n"
+ "with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'tutorial03_cov.pkl'), 'rb') as f:\n"
+ "    cov = pickle.load(f)\n"
+ "covmodel = cov['sand_covmodel']\n"
+ "covparam = cov['sand_covparam']\n\n"
+ "# Load kriging results from Tutorial 04 (for comparison)\n"
+ "krig_path = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'tutorial04_krig.pkl')\n"
+ "krig_available = os.path.exists(krig_path)\n"
+ "if krig_available:\n"
+ "    with open(krig_path, 'rb') as f:\n"
+ "        krig = pickle.load(f)\n"
+ "    zk_ok_mean = krig['zk_ok_mean']\n"
+ "    zk_ok_var  = krig['zk_ok_var']\n"
+ "    print('Kriging results loaded.')\n\n"
+ "print('Hard data:', ch.shape, '  Grid:', ck.shape)\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 1. Load the interval dataset\n\n"
+ "The &#96;IntervalData.txt&#96; file contains 323 soil samples where the sand, silt "
+ "and clay contents are given as intervals of width 20% "
+ "(e.g., sand in [20%, 40%]).\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Read interval data (skip % comment lines)\n"
+ "interval_path = os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'IntervalData.txt')\n"
+ "rows = []\n"
+ "with open(interval_path) as fh:\n"
+ "    for line in fh:\n"
+ "        s = line.strip()\n"
+ "        if s and not s.startswith('%'):\n"
+ "            rows.append([float(v) for v in s.split()])\n\n"
+ "data = np.array(rows)   # (323, 8)\n"
+ "cs      = data[:, :2]   # easting, northing\n"
+ "s_lo    = data[:, 2]    # sand lower bound (%)\n"
+ "s_hi    = data[:, 3]    # sand upper bound (%)\n\n"
+ "print(f'Interval soft data: {cs.shape[0]} locations')\n"
+ "print(f'Sand interval range: [{s_lo.min():.0f}, {s_hi.max():.0f}] %')\n"
+ "print(f'Mean interval width: {np.mean(s_hi - s_lo):.1f} %')\n\n"
+ "# Easting / Northing extents\n"
+ "e_range = cs[:, 0].min(), cs[:, 0].max()\n"
+ "n_range = cs[:, 1].min(), cs[:, 1].max()\n"
+ "print(f'Easting : {e_range[0]:.0f} -- {e_range[1]:.0f} m')\n"
+ "print(f'Northing: {n_range[0]:.0f} -- {n_range[1]:.0f} m')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Visualise hard data and soft data locations\n"
+ "mid_sand = 0.5 * (s_lo + s_hi)  # interval midpoints for colour coding\n\n"
+ "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 7))\n"
+ "# Soft data: circles sized by interval width\n"
+ "widths = s_hi - s_lo\n"
+ "sc_soft = ax.scatter(cs[:, 0], cs[:, 1],\n"
+ "                     c=mid_sand, cmap='hot_r', vmin=0, vmax=60,\n"
+ "                     s=100 + 8 * widths, alpha=0.6,\n"
+ "                     edgecolors='steelblue', linewidths=1.0, label='Interval (soft)')\n"
+ "# Hard data: filled squares\n"
+ "sc_hard = ax.scatter(ch[:, 0], ch[:, 1],\n"
+ "                     c=sand, cmap='hot_r', vmin=0, vmax=60,\n"
+ "                     marker='s', s=50, edgecolors='k', linewidths=0.8,\n"
+ "                     label='Exact (hard)')\n"
+ "plt.colorbar(sc_soft, ax=ax, label='Sand midpoint (%)')\n"
+ "ax.set_title('Falmagne - Hard data (squares) and interval soft data (circles)')\n"
+ "ax.set_xlabel('Easting (m)')\n"
+ "ax.set_ylabel('Northing (m)')\n"
+ "ax.set_aspect('equal')\n"
+ "ax.legend()\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout()\n"
+ "plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 2. Encode intervals as uniform soft PDFs\n\n"
+ "&#96;probaUniform&#96; converts lower/upper bounds into the standard stamps soft-data format:\n\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n"
+ "zs = probaUniform(zlow, zup)\n"
+ "# Returns: [softpdftype=2, nl, limi, probdens]\n"
+ "#   softpdftype : 2 = piecewise-linear PDF\n"
+ "#   nl          : (ns, 1) number of limit points per location\n"
+ "#   limi        : (ns, 2) lower and upper bounds\n"
+ "#   probdens    : (ns, 2) constant probability density\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Encode sand intervals as uniform soft PDFs\n"
+ "zs_soft = probaUniform(s_lo, s_hi)\n"
+ "softpdftype, nl, limi, probdens = zs_soft\n\n"
+ "print(f'softpdftype : {softpdftype}')\n"

+ "print(f'probdens shape: {probdens.shape}')\n"

+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(

+ # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+ """Generate 06_bme_probabilistic_soft_data.ipynb"""

+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "# Tutorial 06 - BME with Full Probabilistic Soft Data\n\n"
+ "**Package:** stamps_v3  \n"
+ "**MATLAB equivalent:** &#96;BMEPROBALIBtutorial.m&#96; (Part 1 - 2D spatial)\n"
+ "**Dataset:** Synthetic dataset generated from the Falmagne covariance model\n\n"
+ "---\n\n"
+ "## Learning objectives\n\n"
+ "1. Generate a **synthetic spatial dataset** using Cholesky simulation (&#96;simuchol&#96;).\n"
+ "2. Encode data as **Gaussian soft PDFs** and **uniform interval PDFs** using "
+ "   &#96;probaGaussian&#96; and &#96;probaUniform&#96;.\n"
+ "3. Run **BME posterior moments** over a spatial grid using &#96;BMEPosteriorMoments&#96;.\n"
+ "4. Compute the **full posterior PDF** at selected locations using &#96;BMEPosteriorPDF_grid&#96;.\n"
+ "5. Compute **credible intervals** (68%, 90%, 99%) using &#96;BMEPosteriorCI&#96;.\n\n"
+ "### Probabilistic vs. interval soft data\n\n"
+ "- **Interval (Tutorial 05)**: uniform PDF over $[z^{lo}, z^{up}]$.\n"
+ "- **Probabilistic (this tutorial)**: any non-negative function $f(z) \\ge 0$ "
+ "  with $\\int f(z)\\,dz = 1$.  This is the most general BME soft data type.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "import sys, os, pickle\n"
+ "import numpy as np\n"
+ "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n"
+ "REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), '..'))\n"
+ "if REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:\n"
+ "    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)\n\n"
+ "from stamps.stats.simulation.simulation import simuchol\n"
+ "from stamps.bme.softconverter import probaGaussian, probaUniform, proba2stat\n"
+ "from stamps.bme.BMEprobaEstimations import (\n"
+ "    BMEPosteriorMoments,\n"
+ "    BMEPosteriorPDF_grid,\n"
+ "    BMEPosteriorCI,\n"
+ ")\n\n"
+ "plt.rcParams.update({'figure.dpi': 110, 'font.size': 10})\n"
+ "DATA_DIR = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'data')\n\n"
+ "# Load covariance model from Tutorial 03\n"
+ "with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'tutorial03_cov.pkl'), 'rb') as f:\n"
+ "    cov = pickle.load(f)\n"
+ "covmodel = cov['sand_covmodel']\n"
+ "covparam = cov['sand_covparam']\n\n"
+ "print('Covariance model:', covmodel)\n"
+ "for m, p in zip(covmodel, covparam):\n"
+ "    print(f'  {m}: {np.round(p, 2)}')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 1. Generate a synthetic spatial dataset\n\n"
+ "We create a controlled experiment on a 15 x 15 grid by simulating from the "
+ "known covariance model.  This allows us to verify our BME estimates against "
+ "the known truth.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Create a 15x15 regular grid\n"
+ "rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=42)\n"
+ "nx, ny = 15, 15\n"
+ "x_sim = np.linspace(0, 28_000, nx)\n"
+ "y_sim = np.linspace(0, 20_000, ny)\n"
+ "XX, YY = np.meshgrid(x_sim, y_sim)\n"
+ "grid_coords = np.column_stack([XX.ravel(), YY.ravel()])\n\n"
+ "# Simulate one realisation from the covariance model (zero-mean Gaussian)\n"
+ "zh_sim, _ = simuchol(grid_coords, covmodel, covparam, ns=1, seed=42)\n"
+ "zh_full   = zh_sim[:, 0]   # (n_grid,) true field\n\n"
+ "print(f'Simulated field shape: {zh_full.shape}')\n"
+ "print(f'True mean : {zh_full.mean():.3f}  (expected 0 for zero-mean)')\n"
+ "print(f'True var  : {zh_full.var():.3f}')\n\n"
+ "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n"
+ "sc = ax.scatter(grid_coords[:, 0], grid_coords[:, 1], c=zh_full,\n"
+ "                cmap='RdYlBu_r', s=80, edgecolors='k', lw=0.3)\n"
+ "plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, label='Simulated Z')\n"
+ "ax.set_title('True simulated field (for verification)')\n"
+ "ax.set_aspect('equal')\n"
+ "ax.set_xlabel('X (m)')\n"
+ "ax.set_ylabel('Y (m)')\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout()\n"
+ "plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 2. Create hard data and soft data subsets\n\n"
+ "From the simulated field we extract:\n\n"
+ "- **Hard data** (exact values): 40 locations randomly selected.\n"
+ "- **Gaussian soft data**: 30 locations with noisy measurements "
+ "  (mean = true value, std = 2 units).\n"
+ "- **Estimation grid**: the remaining locations.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "n_grid = len(grid_coords)\n"
+ "idx_all = rng.permutation(n_grid)\n\n"
+ "n_hard = 40\n"
+ "n_soft = 30\n\n"
+ "idx_hard = idx_all[:n_hard]\n"
+ "idx_soft = idx_all[n_hard:n_hard + n_soft]\n"
+ "idx_est  = idx_all[n_hard + n_soft:]\n\n"
+ "# Hard data\n"
+ "ch_syn = grid_coords[idx_hard]      # (n_hard, 2)\n"
+ "zh_syn = zh_full[idx_hard]          # (n_hard,) exact values\n\n"
+ "# Gaussian soft data: noisy measurements\n"
+ "noise_std = 2.0\n"
+ "cs_syn    = grid_coords[idx_soft]   # (n_soft, 2)\n"
+ "z_soft_mean = zh_full[idx_soft] + rng.normal(0, noise_std, n_soft)  # noisy mean\n"
+ "z_soft_std  = noise_std * np.ones(n_soft)                            # known uncertainty\n\n"
+ "# Estimation grid (remaining locations)\n"
+ "ck_syn  = grid_coords[idx_est]      # estimation coords\n"
+ "z_true  = zh_full[idx_est]          # true values for verification\n\n"
+ "print(f'Hard data     : {n_hard} locations')\n"
+ "print(f'Gaussian soft : {n_soft} locations  (noise std={noise_std})')\n"
+ "print(f'Estimation    : {len(ck_syn)} locations')\n\n"
+ "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n"
+ "ax.scatter(ck_syn[:, 0],  ck_syn[:, 1],  c='lightgrey', s=25, alpha=0.6, label='Estimation')\n"
+ "ax.scatter(cs_syn[:, 0],  cs_syn[:, 1],  c='steelblue', s=60, marker='o',\n"
+ "           edgecolors='navy', lw=0.5, label=f'Gaussian soft (n={n_soft})')\n"
+ "ax.scatter(ch_syn[:, 0],  ch_syn[:, 1],  c='tomato',    s=80, marker='s',\n"
+ "           edgecolors='k',    lw=0.5, label=f'Hard data (n={n_hard})')\n"
+ "ax.set_title('Data configuration')\n"
+ "ax.set_aspect('equal')\n"
+ "ax.set_xlabel('X (m)')\n"
+ "ax.set_ylabel('Y (m)')\n"
+ "ax.legend()\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout()\n"
+ "plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 3. Encode Gaussian soft PDFs with &#96;probaGaussian&#96;\n\n"
+ "&#96;probaGaussian&#96; discretises a Gaussian distribution at each soft data location "
+ "into the stamps piecewise-linear PDF format:\n\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n"
+ "zs = probaGaussian(zmean, zstd)\n"
+ "# Returns: [softpdftype, nl, limi, probdens]\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n"
+ "The resulting PDFs are centred on the noisy measurement with spread proportional "
+ "to the measurement error.\n"
+ ))
+

+

+ "print(f'limi shape  : {limi_g.shape}')\n"
+ "print(f'probdens shape: {pd_g.shape}')\n\n"

+ "print(f'Mean of soft vars  : {s_var.mean():.3f}  (expected ~{noise_std**2:.1f})')\n\n"

+ "    ax.plot(x_i, y_i, 'steelblue', lw=2)\n"

+ "    ax.axvline(z_soft_mean[i], color='steelblue', ls=':', lw=1.5, label='Meas')\n"
+ "    ax.set_title(f'Soft loc {i}')\n"
+ "    ax.set_xlabel('Z')\n"
+ "    if i == 0:\n"

+ "        ax.legend(fontsize=8)\n"

+ "plt.tight_layout()\n"
+ "plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 4. BME posterior moments\n\n"
+ "Combine hard and Gaussian-soft data to compute BME posterior mean and variance "
+ "at all estimation grid nodes.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "nhmax = 10\n"
+ "nsmax = 8\n"
+ "dmax  = 12_000.0\n\n"
+ "print('Running BMEPosteriorMoments (synthetic dataset)...')\n"
+ "result_bme = BMEPosteriorMoments(\n"
+ "    ck_syn,\n"
+ "    ch=ch_syn, cs=cs_syn,\n"
+ "    zh=zh_syn.reshape(-1, 1),\n"

+

+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 5. Posterior PDF at a single location\n\n"
+ "&#96;BMEPosteriorPDF_grid&#96; computes the full posterior PDF $f_k(z)$ at each "

+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Choose a single estimation location near the centre\n"
+ "i_sel = len(ck_syn) // 2\n"

+ "This is the Bayesian analogue of a confidence interval.\n"

+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(

+ # -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
+ """Generate 07_bme_spacetime.ipynb"""
+ import nbformat as nbf
+ 
+ nb = nbf.v4.new_notebook()

+ nb.metadata['language_info'] = {'name': 'python', 'version': '3.9.0'}
+ cells = []
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "# Tutorial 07 - BME in the Space-Time Domain\n\n"
+ "**Package:** stamps_v3  \n"
+ "**MATLAB equivalent:** &#96;BMEPROBALIBtutorial.m&#96; (Part 2 - space-time domain)  \n"
+ "**Dataset:** Synthetic space-time dataset\n\n"
+ "---\n\n"
+ "## Learning objectives\n\n"
+ "1. Extend the spatial framework to **space-time** (2D space + time).\n"
+ "2. Build a **separable space-time covariance model** using &#96;exponentialCST&#96;.\n"
+ "3. Prepare space-time coordinates and data with &#96;valstv2stg&#96; / &#96;valstg2stv&#96;.\n"
+ "4. Run BME posterior moments for a specific **time slice** using &#96;BMEPosteriorMoments&#96;.\n"
+ "5. Visualise BME mean and variance maps for the target time.\n\n"
+ "### Space-time coordinates in stamps_v3\n\n"
+ "Space-time data requires **3-column coordinate arrays**: &#96;[easting, northing, time]&#96;.  "
+ "The &#96;dmax&#96; parameter becomes a 3-element vector &#96;[dmax_space, dmax_time, st_ratio]&#96;:\n\n"
+ "- &#96;dmax_space&#96; — maximum spatial search radius (metres)\n"
+ "- &#96;dmax_time&#96;  — maximum temporal search radius (time units)\n"
+ "- &#96;st_ratio&#96;   — scale factor converting time to spatial units\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "import sys, os, pickle\n"
+ "import numpy as np\n"
+ "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n\n"
+ "REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(os.getcwd(), '..'))\n"
+ "if REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:\n"
+ "    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)\n\n"
+ "from stamps.stats.simulation.simulation import simuchol\n"
+ "from stamps.bme.softconverter import probaGaussian, probaUniform\n"
+ "from stamps.bme.BMEprobaEstimations import BMEPosteriorMoments\n\n"
+ "plt.rcParams.update({'figure.dpi': 110, 'font.size': 10})\n"
+ "DATA_DIR = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'data')\n\n"
+ "# Load covariance model from Tutorial 03\n"
+ "with open(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'tutorial03_cov.pkl'), 'rb') as f:\n"
+ "    cov = pickle.load(f)\n"
+ "covmodel_space = cov['sand_covmodel']\n"
+ "covparam_space = cov['sand_covparam']\n\n"
+ "print('Spatial covariance model:', covmodel_space)\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 1. Build the space-time covariance model\n\n"
+ "A **separable** space-time covariance model factors into the product of "
+ "a spatial and a temporal component:\n\n"
+ "$$C(h_s, h_t) = C_s(h_s) \\cdot C_t(h_t)$$\n\n"
+ "In stamps_v3, we express this as a **nested model** with combined metric distance:\n\n"
+ "$$d_{combined} = h_s + r_{st} \\cdot h_t$$\n\n"
+ "where $r_{st}$ converts time units to spatial units. The &#96;exponentialCST&#96; model "
+ "applies to this combined distance.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Separable space-time covariance model\n"
+ "# For the space-time case we use non-separable CST covariance models\n"
+ "# and encode the space-time ratio in dmax\n\n"
+ "# Covariance sill and ranges from Tutorial 03 + temporal extension\n"
+ "c_nugget = float(covparam_space[0][0])  # nugget sill\n"
+ "c_sill   = float(covparam_space[1][0])  # spatial sill\n"
+ "a_s      = float(covparam_space[1][1])  # spatial range [m]\n\n"
+ "# Temporal model parameters\n"
+ "a_t      = 2.0      # temporal range [days]\n"
+ "st_ratio = a_s / a_t  # spatial-to-temporal ratio (m/day)\n\n"
+ "# Combined model: nugget + exponential (applied to combined s+t distance)\n"
+ "covmodel_st = ['nuggetC', 'exponentialCST']\n"
+ "covparam_st = [(c_nugget,), (c_sill, a_s)]\n\n"
+ "print('Space-time covariance model:', covmodel_st)\n"
+ "print(f'  Nugget : {c_nugget:.3f}')\n"
+ "print(f'  Sill   : {c_sill:.3f}')\n"
+ "print(f'  Spatial range : {a_s:.0f} m')\n"
+ "print(f'  Temporal range: {a_t:.1f} days')\n"
+ "print(f'  ST ratio      : {st_ratio:.1f} m/day')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 2. Simulate a space-time dataset\n\n"
+ "We create a synthetic space-time field over a 10 x 10 spatial grid observed "
+ "at 5 time steps (Days 1-5).\n\n"
+ "**Implementation approach:**  \n"
+ "We simulate the spatial field at each time step independently using &#96;simuchol&#96;, "
+ "adding temporal correlation by a simple AR(1) model:\n\n"
+ "$$Z(s, t) = \\rho \\cdot Z(s, t-1) + \\sqrt{1-\\rho^2} \\cdot \\varepsilon(s, t)$$\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "rng = np.random.default_rng(seed=7)\n\n"
+ "# Spatial grid\n"
+ "nx_st, ny_st = 10, 10\n"
+ "x_st = np.linspace(0, 20_000, nx_st)\n"
+ "y_st = np.linspace(0, 14_000, ny_st)\n"
+ "XX_st, YY_st = np.meshgrid(x_st, y_st)\n"
+ "spatial_grid = np.column_stack([XX_st.ravel(), YY_st.ravel()])  # (100, 2)\n\n"
+ "n_space = len(spatial_grid)\n"
+ "n_time  = 5                     # Days 1 to 5\n"
+ "times   = np.arange(1, n_time + 1, dtype=float)\n\n"
+ "# Temporal AR(1) correlation\n"
+ "rho = np.exp(-1.0 / a_t)        # AR(1) coefficient\n\n"
+ "# Simulate using spatial Cholesky + AR(1) in time\n"
+ "Z_st = np.zeros((n_space, n_time))\n"
+ "eps0, _ = simuchol(spatial_grid, covmodel_space, covparam_space, ns=1, seed=rng)\n"
+ "Z_st[:, 0] = eps0[:, 0]\n"
+ "for t in range(1, n_time):\n"
+ "    eps_t, _ = simuchol(spatial_grid, covmodel_space, covparam_space, ns=1, seed=rng)\n"
+ "    Z_st[:, t] = rho * Z_st[:, t - 1] + np.sqrt(1 - rho**2) * eps_t[:, 0]\n\n"
+ "print(f'Simulated field shape: {Z_st.shape}  ({n_space} locations x {n_time} times)')\n"
+ "print(f'Global mean : {Z_st.mean():.4f}')\n"
+ "print(f'Global var  : {Z_st.var():.4f}')\n\n"
+ "# Plot all time slices\n"
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, n_time, figsize=(18, 3.5))\n"
+ "vz = np.percentile(np.abs(Z_st), 97)\n"
+ "for t_i, ax in enumerate(axes):\n"
+ "    Z_map = Z_st[:, t_i].reshape(ny_st, nx_st)\n"
+ "    im = ax.pcolormesh(x_st, y_st, Z_map, cmap='RdYlBu_r',\n"
+ "                       vmin=-vz, vmax=vz, shading='nearest')\n"
+ "    ax.set_title(f'Day {t_i+1}')\n"
+ "    ax.set_aspect('equal')\n"
+ "    if t_i == 0:\n"
+ "        ax.set_ylabel('Y (m)')\n"
+ "    ax.set_xlabel('X (m)')\n"
+ "plt.colorbar(im, ax=axes[-1], label='Z')\n"
+ "plt.suptitle('Simulated space-time field (Days 1-5)', fontsize=12, y=1.01)\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout()\n"
+ "plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 3. Prepare space-time data\n\n"
+ "Hard data: exact observations at 25 randomly selected space-time points.  \n"
+ "Soft data: noisy Gaussian observations at 20 other space-time points.  \n"
+ "Estimation target: Day 3 (time = 3) over the full spatial grid.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Build all space-time observations as (x, y, t) tuples\n"
+ "n_pts_total = n_space * n_time\n"
+ "# Create full space-time coordinate array\n"
+ "all_coords_st = []\n"
+ "all_vals_st   = []\n"
+ "for t_i, t_val in enumerate(times):\n"
+ "    for s_i in range(n_space):\n"
+ "        all_coords_st.append([spatial_grid[s_i, 0],\n"
+ "                              spatial_grid[s_i, 1],\n"
+ "                              t_val])\n"
+ "        all_vals_st.append(Z_st[s_i, t_i])\n"
+ "\n"
+ "all_coords_st = np.array(all_coords_st)  # (500, 3)\n"
+ "all_vals_st   = np.array(all_vals_st)    # (500,)\n\n"
+ "# Random split into hard and soft data\n"
+ "idx_all_st   = rng.permutation(n_pts_total)\n"
+ "n_hard_st    = 25\n"
+ "n_soft_st    = 20\n"
+ "idx_hard_st  = idx_all_st[:n_hard_st]\n"
+ "idx_soft_st  = idx_all_st[n_hard_st:n_hard_st + n_soft_st]\n\n"
+ "ch_st = all_coords_st[idx_hard_st]    # (n_hard, 3)\n"
+ "zh_st = all_vals_st[idx_hard_st]      # (n_hard,)\n"
+ "\n"
+ "cs_st = all_coords_st[idx_soft_st]    # (n_soft, 3)\n"
+ "noise_s = 1.5\n"
+ "z_soft_st_mean = all_vals_st[idx_soft_st] + rng.normal(0, noise_s, n_soft_st)\n"
+ "z_soft_st_std  = noise_s * np.ones(n_soft_st)\n\n"
+ "# Encode Gaussian soft data\n"
+ "zs_st = probaGaussian(z_soft_st_mean, z_soft_st_std)\n\n"
+ "# Estimation grid: target Day 3\n"
+ "target_time = 3.0\n"
+ "ck_st = np.column_stack([\n"
+ "    spatial_grid,\n"
+ "    target_time * np.ones(n_space)\n"
+ "])  # (n_space, 3)\n\n"
+ "# True values at target time for verification\n"
+ "t_idx = np.where(times == target_time)[0][0]\n"
+ "z_true_day3 = Z_st[:, t_idx]\n\n"
+ "print(f'Hard data    : {n_hard_st} space-time points')\n"
+ "print(f'Soft data    : {n_soft_st} space-time points')\n"
+ "print(f'Estimation   : {n_space} locations at Day {target_time:.0f}')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Visualise data configuration for Day 3\n"
+ "day3_mask_h = ch_st[:, 2] == target_time\n"
+ "day3_mask_s = cs_st[:, 2] == target_time\n\n"
+ "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 6))\n"
+ "Z_true_map = z_true_day3.reshape(ny_st, nx_st)\n"
+ "im = ax.pcolormesh(x_st, y_st, Z_true_map, cmap='RdYlBu_r',\n"
+ "                   vmin=-vz, vmax=vz, shading='nearest', alpha=0.6)\n"
+ "plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label='True Z')\n"
+ "ax.scatter(ch_st[day3_mask_h, 0], ch_st[day3_mask_h, 1],\n"
+ "           c='tomato', s=80, marker='s', edgecolors='k', lw=0.5,\n"
+ "           zorder=4, label='Hard data (Day 3)')\n"
+ "ax.scatter(ch_st[~day3_mask_h, 0], ch_st[~day3_mask_h, 1],\n"
+ "           c='lightcoral', s=40, marker='s', edgecolors='k', lw=0.5,\n"
+ "           alpha=0.5, zorder=3, label='Hard data (other days)')\n"
+ "ax.scatter(cs_st[day3_mask_s, 0], cs_st[day3_mask_s, 1],\n"
+ "           c='steelblue', s=60, marker='o', edgecolors='navy', lw=0.5,\n"
+ "           zorder=4, label='Soft data (Day 3)')\n"
+ "ax.scatter(cs_st[~day3_mask_s, 0], cs_st[~day3_mask_s, 1],\n"
+ "           c='lightblue', s=30, marker='o', edgecolors='navy', lw=0.5,\n"
+ "           alpha=0.5, zorder=3, label='Soft data (other days)')\n"
+ "ax.set_title('Data configuration - target: Day 3')\n"
+ "ax.set_aspect('equal')\n"
+ "ax.set_xlabel('X (m)')\n"
+ "ax.set_ylabel('Y (m)')\n"
+ "ax.legend(fontsize=8, loc='upper right')\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout()\n"
+ "plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 4. BME posterior moments at Day 3\n\n"
+ "We pass the **space-time search neighbourhood** via &#96;dmax&#96; as a 2-element vector:\n\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;python\n"
+ "dmax = np.array([[dmax_space, dmax_time]])\n"
+ "&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n"
+ "The &#96;covmodel&#96; is the space-time model using the CST format, and coordinates "
+ "are 3-column arrays &#96;[x, y, t]&#96;.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "# Space-time neighbourhood parameters\n"
+ "nhmax_st   = 10\n"
+ "nsmax_st   = 8\n"
+ "dmax_space = 15_000.0   # 15 km spatial search\n"
+ "dmax_time  = 2.5        # 2.5 day temporal search\n"
+ "dmax_st    = np.array([[dmax_space, dmax_time]])\n\n"
+ "print('Running space-time BME for Day 3...')\n"
+ "print(f'  nhmax={nhmax_st}, nsmax={nsmax_st}')\n"
+ "print(f'  dmax_space={dmax_space:.0f} m, dmax_time={dmax_time:.1f} days')\n\n"
+ "result_st = BMEPosteriorMoments(\n"
+ "    ck_st,\n"
+ "    ch=ch_st, cs=cs_st,\n"
+ "    zh=zh_st.reshape(-1, 1),\n"
+ "    zs=tuple(zs_st),\n"
+ "    covmodel=covmodel_st,\n"
+ "    covparam=covparam_st,\n"
+ "    order=np.nan,\n"
+ "    nhmax=nhmax_st, nsmax=nsmax_st,\n"
+ "    dmax=dmax_st,\n"
+ ")\n\n"
+ "bme_st_mean = result_st[:, 0]\n"
+ "bme_st_var  = result_st[:, 1]\n\n"
+ "valid_st = ~np.isnan(bme_st_mean)\n"
+ "rmse_st  = np.sqrt(np.mean((bme_st_mean[valid_st] - z_true_day3[valid_st])**2))\n"
+ "print(f'\\nBME estimated {valid_st.sum()} / {n_space} nodes')\n"
+ "print(f'RMSE vs truth: {rmse_st:.4f}')\n"
+ "print(f'Mean variance: {np.nanmean(bme_st_var):.4f}')\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(17, 5))\n\n"
+ "def show_st_map(ax, z_vals, title, cmap='RdYlBu_r', vmin=None, vmax=None, cbar_label='Z'):\n"
+ "    Z_map = z_vals.reshape(ny_st, nx_st)\n"
+ "    vm = vmin if vmin is not None else np.nanpercentile(z_vals, 2)\n"
+ "    vx = vmax if vmax is not None else np.nanpercentile(z_vals, 98)\n"
+ "    im = ax.pcolormesh(x_st, y_st, Z_map, cmap=cmap,\n"
+ "                       vmin=vm, vmax=vx, shading='nearest')\n"
+ "    plt.colorbar(im, ax=ax, label=cbar_label)\n"
+ "    ax.set_title(title)\n"
+ "    ax.set_aspect('equal')\n"
+ "    ax.set_xlabel('X (m)')\n"
+ "    ax.set_ylabel('Y (m)')\n\n"
+ "show_st_map(axes[0], z_true_day3, 'True field - Day 3',\n"
+ "            vmin=-vz, vmax=vz)\n"
+ "show_st_map(axes[1], bme_st_mean, 'BME mean - Day 3',\n"
+ "            vmin=-vz, vmax=vz)\n"
+ "show_st_map(axes[2], bme_st_var,  'BME variance - Day 3',\n"
+ "            cmap='Blues', cbar_label='Variance')\n\n"
+ "# Mark hard/soft data at or near Day 3\n"
+ "for ax in axes[:2]:\n"
+ "    nearby_h = np.abs(ch_st[:, 2] - target_time) &lt;= 1.5\n"

+ "plt.suptitle('Space-time BME estimation at Day 3', fontsize=12, y=1.01)\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout()\n"
+ "plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 5. BME maps across multiple time slices\n\n"
+ "Repeat the BME estimation for each of the 5 time slices to see how the "
+ "estimate evolves through time.\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, 5, figsize=(20, 8))\n\n"
+ "for t_i, t_val in enumerate(times):\n"
+ "    # Estimation grid for this time slice\n"
+ "    ck_t = np.column_stack([\n"
+ "        spatial_grid,\n"
+ "        t_val * np.ones(n_space)\n"

+ "    res_t = BMEPosteriorMoments(\n"
+ "        ck_t,\n"
+ "        ch=ch_st, cs=cs_st,\n"
+ "        zh=zh_st.reshape(-1, 1),\n"
+ "        zs=tuple(zs_st),\n"
+ "        covmodel=covmodel_st,\n"
+ "        covparam=covparam_st,\n"
+ "        order=np.nan,\n"
+ "        nhmax=nhmax_st, nsmax=nsmax_st,\n"
+ "        dmax=dmax_st,\n"
+ "    )\n"
+ "    # True field\n"
+ "    Z_true_t = Z_st[:, t_i]\n"

+ "                f'BME mean - Day {int(t_val)}', vmin=-vz, vmax=vz)\n\n"
+ "plt.suptitle('Space-time BME: true field vs. estimates (all days)', fontsize=12, y=1.01)\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout()\n"
+ "plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 6. Effect of temporal neighbourhood\n\n"
+ "The temporal search radius &#96;dmax_time&#96; controls how much past and future "

+ "the estimate in areas with sparse data but may over-smooth temporal dynamics.\n"

+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_code_cell(

+ 
+ cells.append(nbf.v4.new_markdown_cell(
+ "## 7. Summary\n\n"
+ "| Concept | stamps_v3 implementation |\n"
+ "|---|---|\n"
+ "| 3-D coordinates | &#96;[x, y, t]&#96; as 3-column array |\n"
+ "| Space-time covariance | &#96;exponentialCST&#96; + &#96;nuggetC&#96; |\n"
+ "| Space-time neighbourhood | &#96;dmax = [[dmax_space, dmax_time]]&#96; |\n"

+ "| &#96;simuchol&#96; | Cholesky decomposition | None (unconditional) |\n"

+ "| &#96;simuseqcond&#96; | Sequential Gaussian | Hard data |\n"

+ "real_var   = np.var(Zh_seq[:, 0])\n"
+ "print(f'Model total sill        : {model_sill:.3f}')\n"
+ "print(f'Realisation 1 variance  : {real_var:.3f}')\n\n"
+ "# Histogram comparison\n"
+ "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 4))\n\n"
+ "axes[0].hist(sand,          bins=15, density=True, alpha=0.6,\n"
+ "             label='Hard data', color='tomato')\n"
+ "axes[0].hist(Zh_seq[:, 0],  bins=15, density=True, alpha=0.5,\n"
+ "             label='Simulation 1', color='steelblue')\n"
+ "axes[0].set_xlabel('Sand (%)')\n"
+ "axes[0].set_ylabel('Density')\n"
+ "axes[0].set_title('Histogram comparison')\n"
+ "axes[0].legend()\n\n"
+ "# Q-Q plot\n"
+ "q_hard = np.quantile(sand, np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 50))\n"
+ "q_sim  = np.quantile(Zh_seq[:, 0], np.linspace(0.05, 0.95, 50))\n"
+ "axes[1].plot(q_hard, q_sim, 'o', ms=5, alpha=0.7)\n"
+ "lim = [min(q_hard.min(), q_sim.min()), max(q_hard.max(), q_sim.max())]\n"
+ "axes[1].plot(lim, lim, 'k--', lw=1)\n"
+ "axes[1].set_xlabel('Hard data quantiles')\n"
+ "axes[1].set_ylabel('Simulation quantiles')\n"
+ "axes[1].set_title('Q-Q plot: hard data vs. simulation 1')\n\n"
+ "plt.tight_layout()\n"
+ "plt.show()\n"
+ ))
+

+ "| Function | Conditioning | Scalability | Use case |\n"
+ "|---|---|---|---|\n"
+ "| &#96;simuchol&#96; | None | Small grids (&lt;500) | Reference realisations |\n"
+ "| &#96;simucholcond&#96; | Hard data | Small grids | Exact conditioning |\n"
+ "| &#96;simuseqcond&#96; | Hard data | Large grids | Conditional simulations |\n"
+ "| &#96;simuseqcondInt&#96; | Hard + Interval | Medium grids | Physical constraints |\n\n"
+ "**Key insights:**\n"
+ "- Simulations reproduce global variance; kriging estimates underestimate variance.\n"

The `setup.py` is inside `stamps_v3/stamps/`, which is the installable package directory. To install it into your `bme` conda environment, run:

```bash
conda activate bme
pip install -e /Users/hdragon689/Documents/MyDoc_iCloud/packages/stamps/stamps_v3/stamps/
```

The `-e` flag installs it in **editable (development) mode** — this means Python points directly at the source files, so any changes you make to the code are immediately reflected without reinstalling.

**To verify it worked:**

```bash
conda activate bme
python -c "import stamps; print('stamps OK')"
```

**To also install the optional dependencies used in the tutorials:**

```bash
conda activate bme
pip install nbformat matplotlib scipy numpy pandas
```

**If you already have an older version installed and want to force a clean reinstall:**

```bash
conda activate bme
pip uninstall stamps -y
pip install -e /Users/hdragon689/Documents/MyDoc_iCloud/packages/stamps/stamps_v3/stamps/
```

> **Why `-e` (editable)?** Since you're actively developing `stamps_v3`, editable mode is strongly recommended. Without it, you'd need to re-run `pip install` every time you modify a file.

- # Overview
- STAMPS is a Spatial and Temporal Analysis and Mapping Python Suite that provides state-of-art spatiotemporal analysis algorithms. It supports the mordern spatiotemporal geostatistics - Bayesian Maximum Entropy (BME) which is a powerful tool for incorporating prior information and observations into mapping process under conditions of uncertainty. 
- 
- STAMPS is created and maintained by the [STEMLab](https://stemlab.bse.ntu.edu.tw/wordpress/) at [National Taiwan University](https://www.ntu.edu.tw/english/).

- # Installation
- STAMPS depends on the following packages:
- - [numpy](https://numpy.org)
- - [scipy](https://scipy.org)
- - [pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org)
- - [six](https://pandas.pydata.org)

- - xgboostlss

- 
- Further, the other optional dependencies are recommended to be installed:
- - [matplotlib](https://matplotlib.org) is required for visualization
- - [nlopt](https://nlopt.readthedocs.io/en/latest/) is required for nonlinear optimization
- - [rpy2](https://rpy2.github.io) is required for using R package dlnm
- 
- ## From Binaries
- STAMPS can be installed from pip wheels, if all dependencies can be installed as well:
- 
-     pip intall stamps
- 
- ## From Source
- 
-     git clone https://gitlab.com/STEMLabTW/stamps.git
-     python -m pip install -e stamps
- 
- ## Using optional dlnm dependency
- If you want to do advanced time series analysis with dlnm (Distributed Lag Non-Linear Models) support, install
- - [R](https://www.r-project.org) version 3.4 or above
- - R packages [zoo](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/zoo/index.html), [dlnm](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/dlnm/index.html) [nlme](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nlme/index.html), [mgcv](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/mgcv/index.html)

- &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ # STAMPS — Spatial and Temporal Analysis and Mapping Python Suite
+ 
+ **Version:** 1.0.0  
+ **License:** [GNU General Public License v3.0](LICENSE)  
+ **Maintainer:** [STEMLab](https://stemlab.bse.ntu.edu.tw/wordpress/), National Taiwan University
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Overview
+ 
+ STAMPS is a comprehensive Python library for **spatiotemporal geostatistics**, with a focus on **Bayesian Maximum Entropy (BME)** — a powerful framework for incorporating heterogeneous prior knowledge and soft (uncertain) observations into spatial estimation and mapping under uncertainty.
+ 
+ ### Key capabilities
+ 
+ | Category | Features |
+ |---|---|
+ | **Dependence modelling** | Empirical covariance/variogram estimation, model fitting (WLS, MLE), anisotropy analysis, Linear Model of Coregionalisation (LMC) |
+ | **Variogram models** | Nugget, Exponential, Spherical, Gaussian, Hole-cosine, Hole-sine, Linear, Power, Matérn, Mexican Hat |
+ | **Kriging** | Ordinary/Simple kriging, multivariate cokriging, kriging with Normal Score Transformation (NST) |
+ | **BME estimation** | Posterior moments, full posterior PDF, credible intervals, mode — with hard data, interval soft data, and full probabilistic soft data |
+ | **Soft data encoding** | Uniform (interval), Gaussian, Student-T, piecewise-linear PDFs; neighbourhood selection and combination utilities |
+ | **Space-time** | Separable/non-separable space-time covariance models; space-time BME estimation |
+ | **Simulation** | Cholesky (unconditional/conditional), Sequential Gaussian (unconditional/conditional/interval-constrained), Circular Embedding |
+ | **Analysis** | EOF/PCA, MCA, CCA, Empirical Kalman Filter, Entropy, MEP-PDF, GAM, DLNM, STL decomposition |
+ | **Categorical dependence** | Probability table estimation (&#96;probatablecalc&#96;) for categorical spatial data |
+ | **NST transform** | Normal Score Transformation, Gaussian CDF inversion, back-transformation utilities |
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Package structure
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ stamps/
+ ├── bme/                        # Bayesian Maximum Entropy core
+ │   ├── BMEprobaEstimations.py  # BMEPosteriorMoments, PDF, CI, Mode
+ │   ├── BMEoptions.py           # BME configuration options
+ │   ├── softconverter.py        # Soft data encoding utilities
+ │   ├── bme_transform.py        # Normal Score Transformation
+ │   └── pystks_variable.py      # Variable class
+ ├── models/                     # Covariance and variogram model functions
+ │   └── covmodel.py
+ ├── stest/                      # Spatial estimation
+ │   ├── kriging.py              # kriging, cokriging, cokrigingT
+ │   ├── BMEcatPrior.py          # Categorical BME prior
+ │   └── ...
+ ├── stats/
+ │   ├── dependence/             # Spatial dependence modelling
+ │   │   ├── stcov.py            # Empirical covariance (stcov)
+ │   │   ├── stcovfit.py         # Model fitting (covmodelfit, coregfit)
+ │   │   ├── mlecovfit.py        # Maximum likelihood fitting
+ │   │   ├── anisotropy.py       # Anisotropy estimation
+ │   │   ├── probatablecalc.py   # Categorical dependence
+ │   │   └── probatablefit.py    # Categorical model fitting
+ │   ├── analysis/               # Spatiotemporal analysis
+ │   │   ├── eof.py              # EOF/PCA/HOSVD
+ │   │   ├── pca.py, mca.py, cca.py
+ │   │   ├── ent.py, mepdf.py    # Entropy / MEP-PDF
+ │   │   ├── ekf.py              # Empirical Kalman Filter
+ │   │   ├── gam.py, dlnm.py, stl.py  # R-based (optional)
+ │   │   └── ...
+ │   └── simulation/             # Random field generation
+ │       └── simulation.py       # simuchol, simucholcond, simuseqcond,
+ │                               # simuseqcondInt, simuseqcondME,
+ │                               # simuprobabilistic, simuinterval,
+ │                               # stationary_gaussian_process
+ ├── general/                    # Utility functions
+ │   ├── coord2dist.py           # Distance matrices
+ │   ├── coord2K.py              # Covariance matrix assembly
+ │   ├── neighbours.py           # Neighbourhood selection
+ │   ├── findpairs.py            # Duplicate coordinate detection
+ │   └── valstvgx.py             # Space-time coordinate conversion
+ ├── graph/                      # Visualisation helpers
+ │   ├── dataplot.py             # colorplot, histscatterplot
+ │   └── modelplot.py            # modelplot
+ └── mvn/                        # Multivariate normal integration
+     └── mvn.py                  # QMC integration (mvPro, mvMomVec)
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Installation
+ 
+ ### Requirements
+ 
+ **Core dependencies (installed automatically):**
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ numpy &gt;= 1.21
+ scipy &gt;= 1.7
+ pandas &gt;= 1.3
+ six &gt;= 1.15
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ **Optional dependencies (install separately as needed):**
+ 
+ | Package | Purpose |
+ |---|---|
+ | &#96;matplotlib&#96; | All visualisation functions |
+ | &#96;nlopt&#96; | Nonlinear optimisation for &#96;covmodelfit&#96;, &#96;coregfit&#96; |
+ | &#96;xgboost&#96; + &#96;xgboostlss&#96; | Categorical BME prior (&#96;BMEcatPrior&#96;) |
+ | &#96;rpy2&#96; + R | &#96;gam&#96;, &#96;dlnm&#96;, &#96;stl&#96; time-series decomposition |
+ | &#96;nbformat&#96; | Running/generating the tutorial notebooks |
+ 
+ ### Install from source (recommended for development)
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Clone or navigate to the package root
+ cd /path/to/stamps_v3/stamps
+ 
+ # Install in editable mode into your active environment
+ pip install -e .
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Install into a specific conda environment
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ conda activate bme
+ pip install -e /path/to/stamps_v3/stamps/
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Install optional dependencies
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ pip install matplotlib nlopt xgboost
+ # For R-based functions:
+ pip install rpy2
+ # Install R packages: zoo, dlnm, nlme, mgcv
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ### Verify installation
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ python -c "import stamps; print('stamps OK')"
+ pip show stamps   # should show Version: 1.0.0
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Quick start
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;python
+ import numpy as np
+ from stamps.stest.kriging import kriging
+ from stamps.stats.dependence.stcov import stcov
+ from stamps.stats.dependence.stcovfit import covmodelfit
+ from stamps.bme.BMEprobaEstimations import BMEPosteriorMoments
+ from stamps.bme.softconverter import probaUniform
+ 
+ # --- 1. Fit a covariance model ---
+ lagS       = np.array([500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 6000])
+ lagS_range = 500 * np.ones(5)
+ lag_h, cov_h, n_h, _ = stcov(ch, np.array([[0]]), zh, lagS, lagS_range)
+ 
+ covmodel, covparam = covmodelfit(lag_h, cov_h, n_h,
+                                   ['nuggetC', 'sphericalC'],
+                                   [(5.0,), (80.0, 4000.0)])
+ 
+ # --- 2. Ordinary Kriging ---
+ zk_mean, zk_var = kriging(ck, ch, zh, covmodel, covparam,
+                            nhmax=20, dmax=8000.0, order=0)
+ 
+ # --- 3. BME with interval soft data ---
+ zs = probaUniform(z_low, z_high)
+ result = BMEPosteriorMoments(
+     ck,
+     ch=ch, cs=cs,
+     zh=zh.reshape(-1, 1),
+     zs=tuple(zs),
+     covmodel=covmodel, covparam=covparam,
+     order=np.nan,
+     nhmax=15, nsmax=8,
+     dmax=np.array([[8000.0]]),
+ )
+ bme_mean = result[:, 0]
+ bme_var  = result[:, 1]
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+

+ 
+ ## Tutorials
+ 
+ Interactive Jupyter Notebook tutorials are in the &#96;tutorials/&#96; directory:
+ 
+ | Notebook | Topic |
+ |---|---|
+ | &#96;01_data_loading_and_exploration.ipynb&#96; | Data I/O, histograms, IDW, kernel smoothing |
+ | &#96;02_covariance_and_variogram_models.ipynb&#96; | Covariance/variogram model gallery, categorical dependence |
+ | &#96;03_empirical_statistics_and_covariance_fitting.ipynb&#96; | Empirical covariance, model fitting, NST, LMC (coregfit) |
+ | &#96;04_kriging_and_cokriging.ipynb&#96; | Ordinary kriging, cokriging, kriging with NST |
+ | &#96;05_bme_interval_soft_data.ipynb&#96; | BME with uniform interval soft data |
+ | &#96;06_bme_probabilistic_soft_data.ipynb&#96; | BME with Gaussian soft PDFs, posterior PDF, credible intervals |
+ | &#96;07_bme_spacetime.ipynb&#96; | Space-time BME with CST covariance models |
+ | &#96;08_simulation.ipynb&#96; | Unconditional/conditional random field simulation |
+ 
+ **Run tutorials in order** (each saves intermediate results used by the next).
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ conda activate bme
+ pip install nbformat matplotlib
+ cd tutorials/
+ jupyter lab
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ## Running the test suite
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ cd /path/to/stamps_v3
+ bash run_tests.sh
+ # With coverage report:
+ bash run_tests.sh --cov
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Tests are in &#96;tests/&#96; and cover covariance models, soft data encoding, BME estimation, simulation, and kriging.
+

+ ## Relationship to BMElib (MATLAB)
+ 
+ STAMPS inherits its core spatiotemporal geostatistics engine from
+ **BMElib** ([Serre &amp; Christakos, UNC](https://mserre.sph.unc.edu/BMElib_web/)),
+ the original MATLAB reference implementation of Bayesian Maximum Entropy theory.
+ The fundamental BME mathematics — posterior moment computation, soft data encoding,
+ space-time covariance models, and random field simulation — are all rooted in BMElib.
+ 
+ ### Key improvements over BMElib
+ 
+ | # | Area | BMElib (MATLAB) | STAMPS (Python) |
+ |---|---|---|---|
+ | 1 | **Language &amp; cost** | MATLAB (proprietary licence required) | Python (free, open-source) |
+ | 2 | **All-Gaussian analytical fast-path** | Always runs numerical integration | Detects pure-Gaussian case and returns **exact closed-form** posterior moments, PDF, mode, and credible intervals — no integration needed |
+ | 3 | **Numerical integration** | Standard quadrature | **Quasi-Monte Carlo (QMC)** integration via &#96;scipy.stats.qmc&#96;, providing higher accuracy per sample |
+ | 4 | **Numerical stability** | Standard matrix inversion | &#96;_robust_SVD&#96; / &#96;_robust_pinv&#96; with condition-number thresholding; PSD jitter for near-singular covariance matrices |
+ | 5 | **Adaptive neighbourhood** | Fixed neighbourhood | Automatically detects and expands the neighbourhood when too few data points are found within &#96;dmax&#96; |
+ | 6 | **Non-negativity truncation** | No enforcement | PDF and variance estimates are truncated to be non-negative, preventing physically impossible outputs |
+ | 7 | **Normal Score Transformation** | Separate helper scripts | Fully integrated &#96;bme_transform.py&#96; module with &#96;other2gauss&#96;, &#96;gaussinv&#96;, &#96;gausspdf&#96;, &#96;transformderiv&#96;, &#96;pdfgauss2other&#96; |
+ | 8 | **Multivariate LMC fitting** | &#96;coregfit.m&#96; (basic WLS) | &#96;coregfit&#96; uses **Iterated Alternating Weighted Least Squares (IALS)** with automatic PSD projection of sill matrices |
+ | 9 | **Cokriging with transformation** | &#96;krigingT.m&#96; (univariate only) | &#96;cokrigingT&#96; — generalised to the **multivariate** setting with per-variable reference CDFs |
+ | 10 | **Variogram models** | Covariance models only | Adds a full set of **variogram (&#96;*V&#96;) model functions**: &#96;nuggetV&#96;, &#96;exponentialV&#96;, &#96;sphericalV&#96;, &#96;gaussianV&#96;, &#96;holecosV&#96;, &#96;holesinV&#96;, &#96;linearV&#96;, &#96;powerV&#96; |
+ | 11 | **Categorical dependence** | Not available | &#96;probatablecalc&#96; estimates the empirical **probability table** of categorical spatial data across distance classes |
+ | 12 | **Random number reproducibility** | &#96;rand&#96; / &#96;randn&#96; (global state) | All simulation functions accept a &#96;seed&#96; argument via &#96;numpy.random.default_rng(seed)&#96; for **exact reproducibility** |
+ | 13 | **Parallel processing** | Serial loops | &#96;BMEPosteriorMoments&#96; supports &#96;n_workers &gt; 1&#96; via &#96;ThreadPoolExecutor&#96; for parallel estimation over grid nodes |
+ | 14 | **Analysis toolbox** | Not included | EOF/PCA, MCA, CCA, Empirical Kalman Filter, MEP-PDF, entropy, GAM, DLNM, STL decomposition — far beyond BMElib's scope |
+ | 15 | **Modern Python conventions** | MATLAB 1-based indexing | Strict **0-based indexing**, &#96;numpy&#96;/&#96;scipy&#96; vectorisation, Python type hints, NumPy-style docstrings |
+ 
+ ### BMElib functions translated into STAMPS
+ 
+ The table below maps the original BMElib MATLAB functions to their Python equivalents in STAMPS:
+ 
+ | BMElib (&#96;bmeprobalib&#96;) | STAMPS equivalent |
+ |---|---|
+ | &#96;BMEprobaMoments.m&#96; | &#96;BMEPosteriorMoments&#96; in &#96;bme/BMEprobaEstimations.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;BMEprobaPdf.m&#96; | &#96;BMEPosteriorPDF_grid&#96; in &#96;bme/BMEprobaEstimations.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;BMEprobaMode.m&#96; | &#96;BMEPosteriorMode&#96; in &#96;bme/BMEprobaEstimations.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;BMEprobaCI.m&#96; | &#96;BMEPosteriorCI&#96; in &#96;bme/BMEprobaEstimations.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;probaUniform.m&#96; | &#96;probaUniform&#96; in &#96;bme/softconverter.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;probaGaussian.m&#96; | &#96;probaGaussian&#96; in &#96;bme/softconverter.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;probaStudentT.m&#96; | &#96;probaStudentT&#96; in &#96;bme/softconverter.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;probasplit.m&#96; | &#96;probasplit&#96; in &#96;bme/softconverter.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;probaneighbours.m&#96; | &#96;probaneighbours&#96; in &#96;bme/softconverter.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;probacombinedupli.m&#96; | &#96;probacombineddupli&#96; in &#96;bme/softconverter.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;other2gauss.m&#96; | &#96;other2gauss&#96; in &#96;bme/bme_transform.py&#96; |

+ | &#96;coregfit.m&#96; | &#96;coregfit&#96; in &#96;stats/dependence/stcovfit.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;krigingMP.m&#96; | &#96;cokriging&#96; in &#96;stest/kriging.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;krigingT.m&#96; | &#96;cokrigingT&#96; in &#96;stest/kriging.py&#96; |
+ | &#96;simuchol.m&#96; | &#96;simuchol&#96; in &#96;stats/simulation/simulation.py&#96; |

The README now has a dedicated **"Relationship to BMElib"** section. Here's a summary of the 15 key improvements identified:

1. **Free & open-source** — no MATLAB licence needed
2. **All-Gaussian analytical fast-path** — exact closed-form results for pure-Gaussian cases, completely bypassing numerical integration
3. **Quasi-Monte Carlo integration** — higher accuracy per sample than BMElib's standard quadrature
4. **Numerical stability** — robust SVD/pseudoinverse + PSD jitter prevents failures on near-singular covariance matrices
5. **Adaptive neighbourhood** — automatically expands search when too few neighbours are found
6. **Non-negativity truncation** — prevents physically impossible negative PDFs or variances
7. **Integrated NST module** — `bme_transform.py` bundles the full Normal Score Transformation pipeline
8. **IALS-based LMC fitting** — `coregfit` uses iterative alternating WLS with PSD projection, more robust than BMElib's basic WLS
9. **Multivariate cokrigingT** — generalises BMElib's univariate `krigingT.m` to arbitrary numbers of co-variables
10. **Variogram model family** — adds `*V` functions not present in BMElib
11. **Categorical dependence** — `probatablecalc` for non-continuous data
12. **Reproducible simulation** — `seed` argument via `numpy.random.default_rng`
13. **Parallel processing** — `n_workers` for grid estimation
14. **Broad analysis toolbox** — EOF, EKF, GAM, DLNM, STL etc. far beyond BMElib's scope
15. **Modern Python conventions** — 0-based indexing, type hints, NumPy docstrings
