    "| 4 | Gravel | Coarse aquifer |"
))

# ── 1: Imports ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(code(
    "import sys, os\n"
    "import numpy as np\n"
    "import pandas as pd\n"
    "import matplotlib.pyplot as plt\n"
    "import matplotlib.patches as mpatches\n"
    "from matplotlib.colors import ListedColormap\n"
    "\n"
    "# Locate the repository root two levels up from this notebook\n"
    "HERE      = os.path.abspath(os.path.dirname('.'))\n"
    "REPO_ROOT = os.path.abspath(os.path.join(HERE, '..', '..'))\n"
    "if REPO_ROOT not in sys.path:\n"
    "    sys.path.insert(0, REPO_ROOT)\n"
    "\n"
    "from stamps.stest.BMEcatPrior import BMEcatPrior, BMEcatPriorLOOCV\n"
    "from stamps.bme.BMEcatPdf import BMEcatPdf, MCPcatPdf\n"
    "from stamps.stats.dependence.probatablecalc import (\n"
    "    probatablecalc, adaptive_bins)\n"
    "from stamps.stats.dependence.probatablefit import build_pmodel\n"
    "\n"
    "# Lithology colour scheme\n"
    "LITHO_CODES  = [1, 2, 3, 4]\n"
    "LITHO_LABELS = ['Clay', 'Fine sand', 'Sand', 'Gravel']\n"
    "LITHO_COLORS = ['#8B4513', '#F4A460', '#FFD700', '#4682B4']\n"
    "LITHO_CMAP   = ListedColormap(LITHO_COLORS)\n"
    "\n"
    "DATA_DIR = os.path.join(os.getcwd(), 'data')\n"
    "print('stamps imported OK')\n"
    "print('Data directory:', DATA_DIR)"
))

# ── 2: Load data ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md("## 1. Load data"))

cells.append(code(
    "# Wells: 52 unique boreholes, 7913 depth samples — BME hard data\n"
    "wells = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'pingtung_wells.csv'))\n"
    "print(f'Wells: {wells.shape[0]} rows x {wells.shape[1]} cols')\n"
    "print(wells['LithoCode']\n"
    "      .value_counts().sort_index()\n"
    "      .rename({1:'Clay',2:'Fine sand',3:'Sand',4:'Gravel'}))\n"
    "\n"
    "# Training corpus: stratified subsample from all boreholes for XGBoost\n"
    "train_df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'pingtung_training.csv'))\n"
    "print(f'\\nXGBoost training corpus: {train_df.shape[0]} rows')\n"
    "\n"
    "# Estimation grid: 5 depth levels (−285 to −15 m)\n"
    "grid_df = pd.read_csv(os.path.join(DATA_DIR, 'pingtung_estimation_grid.csv'))\n"
    "print(f'\\nEstimation grid: {grid_df.shape[0]} rows')\n"
    "print('Depth levels (Z):', sorted(grid_df['Z'].round(0).unique()))"
))

# ── 3: Study area ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md("## 2. Study area overview"))

cells.append(code(
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 2, figsize=(13, 5))\n"
    "\n"
    "# Cross-section: well data coloured by lithology\n"
    "ax = axes[0]\n"
    "for code, label, color in zip(LITHO_CODES, LITHO_LABELS, LITHO_COLORS):\n"
    "    m = wells['LithoCode'] == code\n"
    "    ax.scatter(wells.loc[m,'X'], wells.loc[m,'Z'],\n"
    "               c=color, label=label, s=4, alpha=0.6)\n"
    "ax.set_xlabel('Easting (m)')\n"
    "ax.set_ylabel('Depth Z (m)')\n"
    "ax.set_title('Cross-section: lithology vs. easting')\n"
    "ax.legend(fontsize=8, markerscale=3)\n"
    "\n"
    "# Class balance\n"
    "ax2 = axes[1]\n"
    "counts = wells['LithoCode'].value_counts().sort_index()\n"
    "ax2.bar(LITHO_LABELS, counts.values, color=LITHO_COLORS, edgecolor='k')\n"
    "ax2.set_ylabel('Depth samples')\n"
    "ax2.set_title('Class balance (well hard data)')\n"
    "for i, v in enumerate(counts.values):\n"
    "    ax2.text(i, v + 20, str(v), ha='center', fontsize=9)\n"
    "\n"
    "plt.tight_layout()\n"
    "plt.show()"
))

# ── 4: Feature engineering ───────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md(
    "## 3. Feature engineering\n\n"
    "| Feature | Description |\n"
    "|---|---|\n"
    "| `-Z` | Depth below surface (positive = deeper) |\n"
    "| `Height` | Surface elevation (m a.s.l.) |\n"
    "| `Formation Factor` | Resistivity-derived lithology proxy (NaN outside model) |\n"
    "| `inResModel` | Binary flag: 1 = inside resistivity model |\n"
    "| `Testing_Distance` | Distance to nearest test well (m) |\n"
    "| `Corner_Distance_1/2/3` | Distances to basin boundary corners (m) |\n"
    "| `Basin_*` | One-hot encoded basin code (4 columns) |\n\n"
    "XGBoost handles NaN natively, so `Formation Factor` NaN values are "
    "passed directly."
))

cells.append(code(
    "def build_features(df):\n"
    "    \"\"\"Build (n, nf) feature matrix from a dataframe.\"\"\"\n"
    "    d = df.copy()\n"
    "    d['Z'] = -d['Z']   # negate: positive = deeper\n"
    "    basin_dummies = pd.get_dummies(d['Basin'], prefix='Basin')\n"
    "    d = pd.concat([d.drop(columns=['Basin']), basin_dummies], axis=1)\n"
    "    exclude = {'X', 'Y', 'LithoCode'}\n"
    "    feat_cols = [c for c in d.columns if c not in exclude]\n"
    "    return d[feat_cols].values.astype(float), feat_cols\n"
    "\n"
    "# Feature matrices\n"
    "X_train, feat_names = build_features(train_df)\n"
    "y_train = train_df['LithoCode'].values.astype(int)\n"
    "\n"
    "X_well, _  = build_features(wells)\n"
    "y_well     = wells['LithoCode'].values.astype(int)\n"
    "\n"
    "# Align basin columns between well and grid data\n"
    "basin_cols_train = [c for c in feat_names if c.startswith('Basin_')]\n"
    "grid_tmp = grid_df.copy()\n"
    "grid_dummies = pd.get_dummies(grid_tmp['Basin'], prefix='Basin')\n"
    "grid_tmp = pd.concat([grid_tmp.drop(columns=['Basin']), grid_dummies], axis=1)\n"
    "for bc in basin_cols_train:\n"
    "    if bc not in grid_tmp.columns:\n"
    "        grid_tmp[bc] = 0\n"
    "grid_feat_cols = ['Z', 'Height', 'Formation Factor', 'inResModel',\n"
    "                  'Testing_Distance', 'Corner_Distance_1',\n"
    "                  'Corner_Distance_2', 'Corner_Distance_3'] + basin_cols_train\n"
    "grid_tmp['Z'] = -grid_tmp['Z']\n"
    "X_grid = grid_tmp[[c for c in grid_feat_cols if c in grid_tmp.columns]].values.astype(float)\n"
    "\n"
    "print(f'Feature matrix shapes:')\n"
    "print(f'  train:  {X_train.shape}  (XGBoost training corpus)')\n"
    "print(f'  well:   {X_well.shape}   (BME hard data + prior prediction source)')\n"
    "print(f'  grid:   {X_grid.shape}   (estimation locations)')\n"
    "print(f'Features ({len(feat_names)}):', feat_names)"
))

# ── 5: Spatial coordinate arrays ──────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md("## 4. Spatial coordinate arrays for BME"))

cells.append(code(
    "# For BME: use (X, Y, Z) 3-D coordinates\n"
    "cs_bme = wells[['X', 'Y', 'Z']].values      # (ns, 3) hard-data coords\n"
    "ck_bme = grid_df[['X', 'Y', 'Z']].values    # (nk, 3) estimation coords\n"
    "ps_bme = y_well                              # (ns,) integer labels\n"
    "\n"
    "# Station IDs: unique well identified by (X, Y) pair\n"
    "station_ids = (\n"
    "    wells['X'].astype(str) + '_' + wells['Y'].astype(str)\n"
    ").values\n"
    "\n"
    "print(f'cs_bme: {cs_bme.shape}  (hard-data locations)')\n"
    "print(f'ck_bme: {ck_bme.shape}  (estimation grid)')\n"
    "print(f'Unique stations (wells): {len(np.unique(station_ids))}')"
))

# ── 6: Pmodel (depth-only for speed) ──────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md(
    "## 5. Empirical transition-probability model (Pmodel)\n\n"
    "We build the Pmodel in the **vertical** (Z) dimension — most lithological "
    "transitions occur with depth.  We use `adaptive_bins` (equal-pair strategy) "
    "to concentrate bins where data density is highest, then kernel-smooth and "
    "regularise with `build_pmodel`."
))

cells.append(code(
    "# 1-D depth coordinates for the Pmodel\n"
    "cs_1d = wells[['Z']].values      # (ns, 1)\n"
    "ck_1d = grid_df[['Z']].values    # (nk, 1)\n"
    "\n"
    "n_bins  = 20\n"
    "d_max   = 250.0   # maximum vertical separation (m)\n"
    "\n"
    "coord_limit = adaptive_bins(\n"
    "    cs_1d, n_bins=n_bins, d_max=d_max, method='equal_pairs'\n"
    ")\n"
    "print('Adaptive bin edges (m):', np.round(coord_limit, 1))\n"
    "\n"
    "D_emp, P_emp, O_emp = probatablecalc(\n"
    "    cs_1d, y_well, LITHO_CODES, coord_limit\n"
    ")\n"
    "print(f'\\nD_emp: {D_emp.shape}, P_emp: {P_emp.shape}, O_emp: {O_emp.shape}')\n"
    "print('Pair counts (first 6):', O_emp[:6].astype(int))"
))

cells.append(code(
    "n_fit = 60\n"
    "kstd  = 20.0   # kernel smoothing bandwidth (m depth)\n"
    "\n"
    "Pmodel, dmodel, alpha_opt = build_pmodel(\n"
    "    D_emp, P_emp, O_emp,\n"
    "    n_fit=n_fit, n_bins=n_bins, d_max_emp=d_max,\n"
    "    kstd_multiplier=kstd / (d_max / n_bins),\n"
    "    regularize=True, verbose=True,\n"
    ")\n"
    "print(f'\\nPmodel: {Pmodel.shape}  (nc x nc x n_fit)')\n"
    "print(f'dmodel: {dmodel[0]:.1f} – {dmodel[-1]:.1f} m')"
))

cells.append(code(
    "# Diagonal: P(class | same class at distance d)\n"
    "fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(8, 4))\n"
    "for i, (lbl, col) in enumerate(zip(LITHO_LABELS, LITHO_COLORS)):\n"
    "    ax.plot(dmodel, Pmodel[i, i, :], color=col, lw=2, label=lbl)\n"
    "ax.set_xlabel('Vertical separation (m)')\n"
    "ax.set_ylabel('P(same class | same class at origin)')\n"
    "ax.set_title('Diagonal Pmodel — vertical self-transition probabilities')\n"
    "ax.legend()\n"
    "ax.grid(True, alpha=0.3)\n"
    "plt.tight_layout()\n"
    "plt.show()"
))

# ── 7: XGBoostLSS prior ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md(
    "## 6. XGBoostLSS prior estimation\n\n"
    "`BMEcatPrior` trains an XGBoostLSS model with Dirichlet output on the "
    "stratified training corpus (4 992 samples from ~7 100 boreholes) and "
    "predicts smooth class-probability vectors at every estimation grid location.\n\n"
    "> **Note:** `cv_config={'n_trials': 0}` skips hyperparameter tuning "
    "for demonstration speed.  Set `n_trials=50` and `optimization_method='sceua'` "
    "for production runs."
))

cells.append(code(
    "prior_matrix, prior_details = BMEcatPrior(\n"
    "    ck=ck_bme,              # estimation coordinates (shape → output nk)\n"
    "    cs=cs_bme,              # hard-data coordinates\n"
    "    ps=ps_bme,              # hard-data category labels (1-D int)\n"
    "    ck_features=X_grid,     # ancillary features at estimation locations\n"
    "    cs_features=X_well,     # ancillary features at well locations\n"
    "    station_ids=station_ids,\n"
    "    method='xgboostlss',\n"
    "    cv_config={'n_trials': 0},   # set n_trials>0 for hyperparameter tuning\n"
    "    categories=LITHO_CODES,\n"
    "    label_map={1:'Clay', 2:'Fine sand', 3:'Sand', 4:'Gravel'},\n"
    "    feature_labels=feat_names,\n"
    "    verbose=True,\n"
    "    return_details=True,\n"
    ")\n"
    "\n"
    "print(f'\\nprior_matrix shape: {prior_matrix.shape}')\n"
    "print('Row-sum check (first 5):', prior_matrix[:5].sum(axis=1).round(6))\n"
    "print('\\nMean prior across all grid locations:')\n"
    "for lbl, p in zip(LITHO_LABELS, prior_matrix.mean(axis=0)):\n"
    "    print(f'  {lbl:12s}: {p:.3f}')"
))

cells.append(code(
    "# Feature importance\n"
    "fi = prior_details.get('feature_importances', {})\n"
    "if fi:\n"
    "    fi_df = pd.Series(fi).sort_values(ascending=True)\n"
    "    fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(7, 4))\n"
    "    fi_df.plot.barh(ax=ax, color='steelblue')\n"
    "    ax.set_xlabel('Normalised importance (gain)')\n"
    "    ax.set_title('XGBoostLSS — feature importances')\n"
    "    ax.axvline(0, color='k', lw=0.7)\n"
    "    plt.tight_layout()\n"
    "    plt.show()\n"
    "else:\n"
    "    print('Feature importances not available (model did not expose them).')"
))

# ── 8: Prior maps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md("## 7. Prior probability maps at depth −75 m"))

cells.append(code(
    "z_slice = -75.0\n"
    "mask_sl = np.abs(grid_df['Z'] - z_slice) < 1.0\n"
    "ck_sl   = grid_df[mask_sl]\n"
    "pm_sl   = prior_matrix[mask_sl]\n"
    "\n"
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(1, 4, figsize=(16, 4))\n"
    "for j, (lbl, col) in enumerate(zip(LITHO_LABELS, LITHO_COLORS)):\n"

    "    sc = ax.scatter(ck_sl['X'], ck_sl['Y'], c=pm_sl[:, j],\n"
    "                    cmap='RdYlGn', vmin=0, vmax=1, s=20)\n"
    "    ax.scatter(wells['X'], wells['Y'], c='k', s=30,\n"
    "               marker='x', linewidths=1.2, label='Well')\n"
    "    plt.colorbar(sc, ax=ax, fraction=0.04)\n"
    "    ax.set_title(f'P({lbl})  Z=−75 m')\n"
    "    ax.set_xlabel('X (m)')\n"
    "    ax.set_ylabel('Y (m)')\n"
    "    ax.tick_params(labelsize=7)\n"
    "\n"
    "plt.suptitle(\n"
    "    'XGBoostLSS prior class probabilities  (depth −75 m)', fontsize=11, y=1.01\n"
    ")\n"
    "plt.tight_layout()\n"
    "plt.show()"
))

# ── 9: Prior LOOCV ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md(
    "## 8. Prior LOOCV — station-level validation\n\n"
    "`BMEcatPriorLOOCV` performs leave-one-station-out cross-validation.  "
    "Each unique well is held out in turn; the XGBoostLSS model is retrained "
    "on all other wells and the prior is predicted at the held-out depths.\n\n"
    "This is the statistically correct validation strategy for borehole data: "
    "depth samples from the same borehole are highly correlated, so they must "
    "always be on the same side of the train/test split."
))

cells.append(code(
    "loocv = BMEcatPriorLOOCV(\n"
    "    cs=cs_bme,\n"
    "    ps=ps_bme,\n"
    "    cs_features=X_well,\n"
    "    station_ids=station_ids,\n"
    "    method='xgboostlss',\n"
    "    hyperparams=None,       # use defaults; set to tuned params in production\n"
    "    categories=LITHO_CODES,\n"
    "    verbose=True,\n"
    ")\n"
    "\n"
    "print(f'\\nPrior LOOCV accuracy:      {loocv[\"accuracy\"]:.3f}')\n"
    "print(f'Prior LOOCV mean log-lik:  {loocv[\"mean_log_likelihood\"]:.3f}')\n"
    "print('\\nConfusion matrix (rows=true, cols=predicted MAP):')\n"
    "cm_df = pd.DataFrame(\n"
    "    loocv['confusion_matrix'],\n"
    "    index=LITHO_LABELS, columns=LITHO_LABELS\n"
    ")\n"
    "print(cm_df)"
))

# ── 10: MCPcatPdf baseline ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md(
    "## 9. MCPcatPdf — baseline estimation (uniform prior)\n\n"
    "As a baseline, we run `MCPcatPdf` which uses only the spatial "
    "transition probability model (no ancillary information)."
))

cells.append(code(
    "# BME neighbourhood parameters (vertical dimension)\n"
    "nsmax_bme = 6\n"
    "dmax_bme  = 200.0   # metres depth\n"
    "bme_opts  = {'auto_dmax': True}\n"
    "\n"
    "print('Running MCPcatPdf (baseline, no ancillary prior)...')\n"
    "result_mcp = MCPcatPdf(\n"
    "    ck_1d, cs_1d, ps_bme,\n"
    "    dmodel, Pmodel,\n"
    "    nsmax=nsmax_bme, dmax=dmax_bme,\n"
    "    categories=LITHO_CODES,\n"
    "    options=bme_opts,\n"
    ")\n"
    "print(f'MCPcatPdf done: {result_mcp.shape}')\n"
    "\n"
    "map_mcp = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)[np.argmax(result_mcp, axis=1)]"
))

# ── 11: BMEcatPdf with XGBoost prior ──────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md(
    "## 10. BMEcatPdf with XGBoostLSS prior\n\n"
    "We inject the prior via `external_priors`.  The Bayes-factor correction "
    "is applied automatically inside `BMEcatPdf`:\n\n"
    "$$\n"
    "q_{\\text{BF}}(c_k) \\propto \\frac{p_{\\text{prior}}(c_k)}{p_{\\text{global}}(c_k)}\n"
    "\\cdot \\prod_{s} P(c_s \\mid c_k)\n"
    "$$\n\n"
    "where $p_{\\text{global}}(c_k)$ is automatically derived from the "
    "training data marginal proportions."
))

cells.append(code(
    "print('Running BMEcatPdf with XGBoostLSS prior...')\n"
    "result_bme_xgb = BMEcatPdf(\n"
    "    ck_1d, cs_1d, ps_bme,\n"
    "    dmodel, Pmodel,\n"
    "    nsmax=nsmax_bme, dmax=dmax_bme,\n"
    "    categories=LITHO_CODES,\n"
    "    options=bme_opts,\n"
    "    external_priors=prior_matrix,\n"
    ")\n"
    "print(f'BMEcatPdf done: {result_bme_xgb.shape}')\n"
    "\n"
    "map_bme_xgb = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)[np.argmax(result_bme_xgb, axis=1)]"
))

# ── 12: Comparison maps ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md(
    "## 11. MAP lithology maps — 5 depth levels, 2 methods"
))

cells.append(code(
    "z_levels = sorted(grid_df['Z'].round(0).unique())\n"
    "n_z = len(z_levels)\n"
    "\n"
    "fig, axes = plt.subplots(2, n_z, figsize=(4 * n_z, 7))\n"
    "\n"
    "method_rows = [\n"
    "    ('MCP (baseline)', map_mcp),\n"
    "    ('BME + XGBoostLSS prior', map_bme_xgb),\n"
    "]\n"
    "\n"
    "for row_i, (title, map_arr) in enumerate(method_rows):\n"
    "    for col_i, z_val in enumerate(z_levels):\n"
    "        ax = axes[row_i, col_i]\n"
    "        z_mask = np.abs(grid_df['Z'].values - z_val) < 1.0\n"
    "        c_idx  = [LITHO_CODES.index(int(v)) for v in map_arr[z_mask]]\n"
    "        ax.scatter(\n"
    "            grid_df['X'].values[z_mask],\n"
    "            grid_df['Y'].values[z_mask],\n"
    "            c=c_idx, cmap=LITHO_CMAP, vmin=-0.5, vmax=3.5,\n"
    "            s=18, edgecolors='none',\n"
    "        )\n"
    "        ax.scatter(wells['X'], wells['Y'], c='k', s=15, marker='+')\n"
    "        ax.set_title(f'Z={int(z_val)} m', fontsize=9)\n"
    "        ax.tick_params(labelsize=6)\n"
    "        if col_i == 0:\n"
    "            ax.set_ylabel(title, fontsize=8)\n"
    "\n"
    "patches = [mpatches.Patch(color=c, label=l)\n"
    "           for c, l in zip(LITHO_COLORS, LITHO_LABELS)]\n"
    "fig.legend(handles=patches, loc='lower center', ncol=4,\n"
    "           fontsize=9, bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.04))\n"
    "fig.suptitle('MAP lithology — 5 depth levels', fontsize=12, y=1.01)\n"
    "plt.tight_layout()\n"
    "plt.show()"
))

# ── 13: LOOCV comparison ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────
cells.append(md(
    "## 12. LOOCV comparison — MCP vs BMEcatPdf (XGBoost prior)\n\n"
    "We evaluate both estimators using station-level LOOCV on the well data "
    "(in 1-D depth).  For each held-out station the XGBoost prior is "
    "retrained on the remaining stations to avoid data leakage."
))

cells.append(code(
    "import time\n"
    "\n"
    "def station_loocv(method_fn, cs_1d, ck_1d, ps, dmodel, Pmodel,\n"
    "                  station_ids, categories, nsmax, dmax, options,\n"
    "                  use_xgb_prior=False, cs_features=None):\n"
    "    \"\"\"Station-level LOOCV for any BMEcatPdf-compatible estimator.\"\"\"\n"
    "    unique_st = np.unique(station_ids)\n"
    "    all_post, all_true = [], []\n"
    "    for st in unique_st:\n"
    "        tr = station_ids != st\n"
    "        te = station_ids == st\n"
    "        ck_te = cs_1d[te]; cs_tr = cs_1d[tr]; ps_tr = ps[tr]; ps_te = ps[te]\n"
    "        ext = None\n"
    "        if use_xgb_prior and cs_features is not None:\n"
    "            ext, _ = BMEcatPrior(\n"
    "                ck=cs_bme[te], cs=cs_bme[tr], ps=ps_tr,\n"
    "                ck_features=cs_features[te],\n"
    "                cs_features=cs_features[tr],\n"
    "                method='xgboostlss',\n"
    "                cv_config={'n_trials': 0},\n"
    "                categories=categories, verbose=False,\n"
    "                return_details=True,\n"
    "            )\n"
    "        post = method_fn(\n"
    "            ck_te, cs_tr, ps_tr, dmodel, Pmodel,\n"
    "            nsmax=nsmax, dmax=dmax, categories=categories,\n"
    "            options=options, external_priors=ext,\n"
    "        )\n"
    "        all_post.append(post)\n"
    "        all_true.append(ps_te)\n"
    "    post_all = np.vstack(all_post)\n"
    "    true_all = np.concatenate(all_true)\n"
    "    cats = np.asarray(categories)\n"
    "    acc = float(np.mean(cats[np.argmax(post_all, axis=1)] == true_all))\n"
    "    ti  = np.searchsorted(categories, true_all)\n"
    "    mll = float(np.mean(np.log(np.clip(\n"
    "        post_all[np.arange(len(true_all)), ti], 1e-15, None))))\n"
    "    return acc, mll\n"
    "\n"
    "print('Running station-level LOOCV (this may take a few minutes)...')\n"
    "\n"
    "t0 = time.perf_counter()\n"
    "acc_mcp, mll_mcp = station_loocv(\n"
    "    MCPcatPdf, cs_1d, ck_1d, ps_bme, dmodel, Pmodel,\n"
    "    station_ids, LITHO_CODES, nsmax_bme, dmax_bme, bme_opts)\n"
    "t_mcp = time.perf_counter() - t0\n"
    "print(f'MCP done ({t_mcp:.1f} s): acc={acc_mcp:.3f}  mll={mll_mcp:.3f}')\n"
    "\n"
    "t0 = time.perf_counter()\n"
    "acc_xgb, mll_xgb = station_loocv(\n"
    "    BMEcatPdf, cs_1d, ck_1d, ps_bme, dmodel, Pmodel,\n"
    "    station_ids, LITHO_CODES, nsmax_bme, dmax_bme, bme_opts,\n"
    "    use_xgb_prior=True, cs_features=X_well)\n"
    "t_xgb = time.perf_counter() - t0\n"
    "print(f'BME+XGBoost done ({t_xgb:.1f} s): acc={acc_xgb:.3f}  mll={mll_xgb:.3f}')"
))

cells.append(code(

```diff
- 
+ # Pingtung Plain Lithology Estimation
+ ## Application report — stamps BME categorical workflow
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### Overview
+ 
+ This example demonstrates how to estimate the **3-D subsurface lithology** of
+ the **Pingtung Plain**, southern Taiwan, using the &#96;stamps&#96; Python package.
+ The Pingtung Plain is an elongated alluvial fan complex ~70 km long and ~30 km
+ wide, underlain by Quaternary sediments that form the primary aquifer system
+ for the region.  Precise knowledge of lithological facies (clay, fine sand,
+ sand, gravel) is essential for groundwater resource management and land
+ subsidence assessment.
+ 
+ The estimation integrates two sources of information:
+ 
+ | Source | Description | Role |
+ |---|---|---|
+ | **Borehole logs** | 52 monitoring wells (~7 900 depth samples) | Spatial hard data for BME |
+ | **Ancillary covariates** | Depth, elevation, resistivity formation factor, basin geometry | Input to XGBoostLSS prior |
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### Dataset
+ 
+ | File | Rows | Description |
+ |---|---|---|
+ | &#96;data/pingtung_wells.csv&#96; | 7 913 | Well depth samples — BME hard data |
+ | &#96;data/pingtung_training.csv&#96; | ~5 000 | Stratified subsample of all boreholes — XGBoost training corpus |
+ | &#96;data/pingtung_estimation_grid.csv&#96; | ~675 | Regular grid at 5 depth levels — estimation targets |
+ 
+ All files are CSV with columns:
+ 
+ | Column | Unit | Description |
+ |---|---|---|
+ | &#96;X&#96;, &#96;Y&#96; | m (TWD97) | Horizontal coordinates |
+ | &#96;Z&#96; | m | Depth below sea level (negative values) |
+ | &#96;Height&#96; | m a.s.l. | Surface elevation |
+ | &#96;LithoCode&#96; | — | Lithology class: 1=Clay, 2=Fine sand, 3=Sand, 4=Gravel |
+ | &#96;Basin&#96; | — | Basin sub-region code |
+ | &#96;Formation Factor&#96; | — | Resistivity-derived lithological proxy (NaN outside model domain) |
+ | &#96;inResModel&#96; | 0/1 | Whether location falls inside the resistivity model domain |
+ | &#96;Testing_Distance&#96; | m | Distance to nearest test well |
+ | &#96;Corner_Distance_1/2/3&#96; | m | Distances to three basin boundary reference points |
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### Method
+ 
+ The estimation pipeline follows four stages:
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ Borehole logs ──► Pmodel (vertical transition probabilities)
+                         │
+ Ancillary covariates ──► XGBoostLSS prior ──► BMEcatPdf ──► MAP lithology
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ #### Stage 1 — Empirical transition-probability model (Pmodel)
+ 
+ The spatial categorical dependence is quantified by a bivariate probability
+ table &#96;P(c₂ | c₁, d)&#96; — the probability that lithology class c₂ occurs at a
+ separation *d* given that class c₁ occurs at the origin.
+ 
+ - **&#96;probatablecalc&#96;** computes the empirical table using an adaptive
+   equal-pair binning strategy (denser bins at short distances, coarser at
+   long distances).
+ - **&#96;build_pmodel&#96;** kernel-smooths the raw table and applies Empirical-Bayes
+   pseudocount regularisation to stabilise cells with few data pairs.
+ 
+ #### Stage 2 — XGBoostLSS prior
+ 
+ &#96;BMEcatPrior(method='xgboostlss')&#96; trains an
+ [XGBoostLSS](https://statmachines.github.io/XGBoostLSS/) model with a
+ **Dirichlet distributional response**.  Unlike a standard classification tree
+ that outputs a single hard label, XGBoostLSS models the full Dirichlet
+ concentration parameters, producing calibrated class-probability vectors that
+ honour the simplex constraint (probabilities sum to 1).
+ 
+ Features used:
+ 
+ | Feature | Physical meaning |
+ |---|---|
+ | −Z | Depth (positive = deeper) |
+ | Height | Surface elevation |
+ | Formation Factor | Proxy for aquifer vs. aquitard |
+ | inResModel | Inside resistivity model domain? |
+ | Testing_Distance | Proximity to test wells |
+ | Corner_Distance_1/2/3 | Basin geometry descriptors |
+ | Basin_* (one-hot) | Sub-basin membership |
+ 
+ #### Stage 3 — BMEcatPdf with Bayes-factor correction
+ 
+ &#96;BMEcatPdf(external_priors=prior_matrix)&#96; applies the Bayesian Maximum
+ Entropy update with the XGBoostLSS prior.  The Bayes-factor correction
+ prevents double-counting of the global class frequency:
+ 
+ $$q_{\text{BF}}(c_k) \propto \frac{p_{\text{prior}}(c_k)}{p_{\text{global}}(c_k)}
+ \cdot \prod_{s \in \mathcal{N}(k)} P(c_s \mid c_k)$$
+ 
+ where:
+ - $p_{\text{prior}}(c_k)$ — XGBoostLSS prediction at location $k$
+ - $p_{\text{global}}(c_k)$ — global marginal (training class proportions), computed automatically
+ - $P(c_s \mid c_k)$ — transition probability from Pmodel
+ 
+ #### Stage 4 — Validation
+ 
+ Station-level leave-one-out cross-validation (LOOCV) is used throughout:
+ 
+ - **Prior validation**: &#96;BMEcatPriorLOOCV&#96; — each well is held out; the
+   XGBoostLSS model is retrained on all other wells.
+ - **BME validation**: &#96;station_loocv&#96; — each well is held out; both the
+   XGBoostLSS prior *and* the BME local neighbourhood are estimated on the
+   remaining wells.
+ 
+ Station-level splits (rather than sample-level) are critical: depth samples
+ from the same borehole are strongly correlated and must always sit on the
+ same side of the train/test boundary.
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### Results
+ 
+ See [&#96;pingtung_lithology_bme.ipynb&#96;](pingtung_lithology_bme.ipynb) for the
+ full interactive results.  Expected outcomes:
+ 
+ - **XGBoostLSS prior** produces spatially continuous class-probability maps
+   that coherently respect depth gradients and basin structure.
+ - **Bayes-factor-corrected &#96;BMEcatPdf&#96;** refines the prior using local
+   borehole transition-probability information, improving accuracy relative to
+   the MCP-only baseline.
+ - **Feature importance** analysis identifies depth (−Z) and resistivity
+   formation factor as the dominant predictors.
+ - **Station LOOCV** provides an unbiased estimate of generalisation
+   performance for both the prior and the full BME estimate.
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### How to run
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;bash
+ # Activate the stamps environment
+ conda activate bme
+ 
+ # Install stamps in editable mode (if not already installed)
+ pip install -e /path/to/stamps_v3
+ 
+ # Launch the notebook
+ cd examples/pingtung_lithology
+ jupyter lab pingtung_lithology_bme.ipynb
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ Dependencies (all satisfied by the &#96;stamps&#96; conda/pip environment):
+ 
+ - &#96;stamps&#96; (this package)
+ - &#96;numpy&#96;, &#96;scipy&#96;, &#96;pandas&#96;, &#96;matplotlib&#96;
+ - &#96;xgboost &gt;= 2.0&#96;
+ - &#96;xgboostlss&#96;
+ - &#96;optuna&#96; (for hyperparameter tuning with &#96;n_trials &gt; 0&#96;)
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### File structure
+ 
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ examples/pingtung_lithology/
+ ├── README.md                        ← this file
+ ├── pingtung_lithology_bme.ipynb     ← main tutorial notebook
+ └── data/
+     ├── pingtung_wells.csv           ← BME hard data (52 wells, 7 913 samples)
+     ├── pingtung_training.csv        ← XGBoost training corpus (~5 000 samples)
+     └── pingtung_estimation_grid.csv ← estimation grid (5 depth levels)
+ &#96;&#96;&#96;
+ 
+ ---
+ 
+ ### References
+ 
+ - Serre, M. L., &amp; Christakos, G. (1999). Modern geostatistics: computational
+   BME analysis in the light of uncertain physical knowledge — the Equus Beds
+   study. *Stochastic Environmental Research and Risk Assessment*, 13(1), 1–26.
+ - Menze, B. H., et al. (2011). A comparison of random forest and its
+   Gini importance with standard chemometric methods for the feature selection
+   and classification of spectral data. *BMC Bioinformatics*, 12, 1–16.
+ - März, A., et al. (2023). XGBoostLSS — an extension of XGBoost to
+   probabilistic forecasting. *arXiv preprint arXiv:2208.09803*.
+ - bmelib: &lt;https://mserre.sph.unc.edu/BMELIB_web/&gt;
+ 
```

</details>

</tool-use>

The fix is applied. Here's what was wrong and what was changed:

**Root cause:** `probatablecalc(coord, value, coord_limit, ...)` expects `value` to be a **2-D one-hot matrix** of shape `(n, nc)` — one column per category. The notebook was passing the raw 1-D integer label array `y_well` as `value` and `LITHO_CODES` as `coord_limit` (a positional-argument shift bug), causing `value.shape[1]` to fail with `IndexError: tuple index out of range`.

**Fix in Cell 11:** One-hot encode `y_well` into `ps_onehot` before the call, and drop the erroneous `LITHO_CODES` positional argument:

```python
# probatablecalc expects a 2-D one-hot (or soft-PDF) matrix, not integer labels
cats_arr  = np.asarray(LITHO_CODES)                                # [1, 2, 3, 4]
ps_onehot = (y_well[:, None] == cats_arr[None, :]).astype(float)  # (ns, 4)

D_emp, P_emp, O_emp = probatablecalc(cs_1d, ps_onehot, coord_limit)
```

This is exactly the same pattern used in `tutorials/09_bme_categorical.ipynb` (line 265): `ps = (code[:, None] == categories[None, :]).astype(float)`.

Now I have a complete picture of both issues. Let me give a thorough answer.

---

## 1. Is it reasonable that XGBoostLSS tuning "failed"?

Yes, this is **expected and by design**. The notebook uses `cv_config={'n_trials': 0}`, which explicitly requests zero Optuna trials. Looking at `_tune_xgboostlss_native` (line 584):

```python
n_trials = cv_config.get("n_trials", 50)
```

When `n_trials=0`, `xgblss_tuner.hyper_opt(...)` is called with `n_trials=0` — Optuna runs zero trial iterations and reports "No trials are completed yet." The `except` clause catches this and warns:

> *"XGBoostLSS native tuning failed (No trials are completed yet.); using defaults."*

Then it falls back to `DEFAULT_XGBOOSTLSS_PARAMS`. So no tuning happens and default hyperparameters are used. This is **intentional for the demo notebook** — the comment says *"skip tuning for speed"*. The model trains correctly with default params; it just isn't optimised.

## 2. Is the prior LOOCV the right validation strategy?

Your proposed approach (80/20 hold-out + 5-fold CV for tuning) and the existing station-level LOOCV serve **different purposes**. Here is the full conceptual picture:

### Three distinct objectives

| Objective | Correct approach |
|---|---|
| **A. Tune hyperparameters** | Inner k-fold CV on the training set only |
| **B. Select / compare models** (e.g. XGBoostLSS vs. XGBoost vs. baseline) | Outer validation on a held-out test set **or** nested CV |
| **C. Report unbiased generalisation accuracy** | Outer LOOCV or k-fold using station-level splits |

### Why station-level LOOCV is correct for borehole data

The core issue is **depth-sample correlation**: a single borehole at coordinates (X, Y) may contribute hundreds of depth samples, all of which are spatially correlated. If you do a random 80/20 split at the **sample level**, some depth samples from the same borehole land in the training set and some in the test set — the test set is no longer independent and accuracy will be **badly overestimated**.

**Station-level** splits guarantee the held-out test set contains only boreholes the model has never seen. This is the only split that gives an unbiased estimate of generalisation to a **new, unseen well location**.

### What the current `BMEcatPriorLOOCV` actually does (and its limitation)

Looking at line 1386:
```python
cv_config={"n_trials": 0},   # no inner tuning in LOOCV
```

The current LOOCV **never re-tunes** hyperparameters per fold — it uses whatever `hyperparams` you pass in (or defaults if `None`). This is a pragmatic shortcut: full nested CV (tune inside each fold) on 52 stations × tuning would be prohibitively slow.

### Recommended two-stage workflow

Your intuition is correct. The proper workflow is:

**Stage 1 — Hyperparameter tuning (once, on full training set with inner CV):**

```python
# Tune once using the FULL dataset with station-grouped k-fold
prior_tuned, details = BMEcatPrior(
    ck=ck_bme, cs=cs_bme, ps=ps_bme,
    ck_features=X_grid, cs_features=X_well,
    station_ids=station_ids,
    method='xgboostlss',
    cv_config={
        'n_trials': 50,              # Optuna trials
        'n_splits': 5,               # 5-fold station-grouped CV for scoring each trial
        'max_minutes': 15,
    },
    return_details=True,
)
best_params = details['hyperparameters']
```

**Stage 2 — Unbiased accuracy estimate (LOOCV with fixed hyperparams from Stage 1):**

```python
# Now evaluate with the tuned params fixed — no inner re-tuning per fold
loocv = BMEcatPriorLOOCV(
    cs=cs_bme, ps=ps_bme, cs_features=X_well,
    station_ids=station_ids,
    method='xgboostlss',
    hyperparams=best_params,   # ← fixed, no re-tuning inside LOOCV
    categories=LITHO_CODES,
    verbose=True,
)
```

This is **not exactly** the "train 80% / test 20%" strategy you described — that would use only one specific split. Station-level LOOCV uses all 52 stations as test sets in turn, giving a much more robust accuracy estimate. The "80/20 hold-out" is better as a quick sanity check when you have many stations, but with only 52 wells LOOCV is preferable because every station contributes to the validation.

### Summary of recommendations

| Issue | Current notebook | Recommended |
|---|---|---|
| Hyperparameter tuning | `n_trials=0` (skipped, uses defaults) | Set `n_trials=50` for production |
| Tuning CV strategy | N/A (no tuning) | Station-grouped 5-fold inner CV (already implemented via `_tune_xgboostlss_native`) |
| LOOCV | Re-trains model per fold with default params | Pass `hyperparams=best_params` from Stage 1 so LOOCV reflects tuned model performance |
| Train/test split | Sample-level would be wrong here | Station-level LOOCV is correct — prevents depth-sample leakage |

In short: **`n_trials=0` is correct for a quick demo**; for a production run, tune first (Stage 1) then validate with fixed params (Stage 2). Switching to agent mode will be needed if you want me to update the notebook cells to implement this two-stage workflow.
